FILE: server/llmretry.go

package server

import (
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/agent"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

// Server-side resolution of the retry policy; see docs/llm-retry-design.md. Of the five layers:
//   - connect / empty response / same-provider safe window "follow the endpoint": every LLM
//     profile can override the global default (an empty profile field inherits the global; if the global is unset too, the built-in default applies);
//   - circuit breaker / intent re-run are process-wide — there is only one global copy.
//
// The global policy reads one settings row from the DB; its call sites are all on low-frequency
// paths (building providers, work wrap-up, saving profiles), so another cache layer is not worth
// it. Circuit-breaker parameters are the exception — they are read on every failure path, so applyRetryPolicy pushes them into the Registry.

// retryPolicy reads the global policy; a nil DB yields the zero policy (all
// layers on their built-in defaults).
func (s *Server) retryPolicy() db.LLMRetryPolicy {
	if s.m == nil || s.m.pg == nil {
		return db.LLMRetryPolicy{}
	}
	return s.m.pg.LLMRetryPolicy()
}

// resolveRetry layers one profile's override on top of the global policy and
// converts the result into the form agent.Config carries. Rules combine field by
// field, so a profile that only pins an interval still inherits the global count.
func resolveRetry(o db.RetryOverride, pol db.LLMRetryPolicy) agent.RetryConfig {
	connect := o.Connect.Or(pol.Connect)
	empty := o.Empty.Or(pol.Empty)
	stream := o.Stream.Or(pol.Stream)
	return agent.RetryConfig{
		// The counts keep their raw "0=default / negative=off" semantics here: the
		// SDK's MaxRetries / EmptyResponseRetries are fully isomorphic to this — let it parse them itself.
		ConnectAttempts: connect.Attempts, ConnectInterval: connect.Interval(),
		EmptyAttempts: empty.Attempts, EmptyInterval: empty.Interval(),
		StreamAttempts: stream.Attempts, StreamInterval: stream.Interval(),
	}
}

// applyProfileRetry fills cfg.Retry for a profile read from the DB.
func (s *Server) applyProfileRetry(cfg *agent.Config, p *db.LLMProfile) {
	if p == nil {
		return
	}
	cfg.Retry = resolveRetry(p.Retry, s.retryPolicy())
}

// Defaults for circuit breaking (pool cool-down), identical to the llmpool built-ins — overridden here only when the user has set a value.
// Intent re-run defaults are engine.go's modelErrorRetries / modelErrorRetryBackoff.

// applyRetryPolicy pushes the process-wide layers of the policy into the objects
// that consume them on a hot path: the circuit-breaker registry. Called at
// startup and whenever the policy is saved.
func (s *Server) applyRetryPolicy() {
	pol := s.retryPolicy()
	if s.llmHealth != nil {
		s.llmHealth.SetPolicy(pol.Breaker.Attempts, pol.Breaker.Interval())
	}
}

// modelErrorRetryPolicy resolves the intent-level replay knobs (layer ⑤): how
// many times a model_error work is re-run and how long to back off between runs.
func (e *Engine) modelErrorRetryPolicy() (retries int, backoff time.Duration) {
	retries, backoff = modelErrorRetries, modelErrorRetryBackoff
	if e == nil || e.m == nil || e.m.pg == nil {
		return retries, backoff
	}
	rule := e.m.pg.LLMRetryPolicy().Intent
	if rule.Attempts != 0 {
		retries = max(rule.Attempts, 0)
	}
	if d := rule.Interval(); d > 0 {
		backoff = d
	}
	return retries, backoff
}

// emptyTurnNudgeLimit resolves how many empty-turn continuations one work may
// inject (see steerHooks.Stop). It deliberately reuses layer ②'s knob — "empty-response
// retry count": the two are two means to the same end. The SDK layer handles "not a single
// content block" by resending the very same request; this one handles "only thinking, neither
// body nor tools" by appending an instruction so the model continues from its existing thinking
// (a verbatim resend is pointless for an idle turn dictated by the shape of the context). The
// emptiness criteria differ because the SDK goes by "has any event been yielded", and thinking
// increments are themselves events — but a user configuring "how many empty-response retries" means "retry once more when the model produced nothing substantive", so sharing one count across both layers matches that mental model.
//
// Reads the global policy rather than a profile's override: a run may switch profiles
// mid-way due to failover, while this is the total gate for the whole intent and must not change with the endpoint. Semantics mirror the SDK's emptyRetries():
// 0 = the default defaultEmptyTurnNudges; -1 (negative) = disable idle-turn continuation; >0 = use that value.
func (e *Engine) emptyTurnNudgeLimit() int {
	if e == nil || e.m == nil || e.m.pg == nil {
		return defaultEmptyTurnNudges
	}
	switch n := e.m.pg.LLMRetryPolicy().Empty.Attempts; {
	case n == 0:
		return defaultEmptyTurnNudges
	case n < 0:
		return 0
	default:
		return n
	}
}

package server

import (
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/agent"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

// With no configuration at all, the resolved result must be all zeros — i.e. the
// built-in defaults of the SDK and task_llm, byte-for-byte identical to before the "configurable retries" feature landed.
func TestResolveRetryUnconfigured(t *testing.T) {
	got := resolveRetry(db.RetryOverride{}, db.LLMRetryPolicy{})
	if got != (agent.RetryConfig{}) {
		t.Fatalf("resolveRetry=%+v, want zero", got)
	}
	retries, backoff := sameProviderRetryPolicy(got)
	if retries != sameProviderStreamRetries {
		t.Fatalf("retries=%d, want %d", retries, sameProviderStreamRetries)
	}
	if d := backoff(1); d != time.Second {
		t.Fatalf("backoff(1)=%v, want 1s (the default ladder)", d)
	}
}

// The global policy applies to a profile that overrides nothing.
func TestResolveRetryFromGlobal(t *testing.T) {
	pol := db.LLMRetryPolicy{
		Connect: db.RetryRule{Attempts: 5, IntervalMS: 2000},
		Empty:   db.RetryRule{Attempts: -1},
		Stream:  db.RetryRule{Attempts: 4, IntervalMS: 1500},
	}
	got := resolveRetry(db.RetryOverride{}, pol)
	want := agent.RetryConfig{
		ConnectAttempts: 5, ConnectInterval: 2 * time.Second,
		EmptyAttempts:  -1,
		StreamAttempts: 4, StreamInterval: 1500 * time.Millisecond,
	}
	if got != want {
		t.Fatalf("resolveRetry=%+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}
	retries, backoff := sameProviderRetryPolicy(got)
	if retries != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("retries=%d, want 4", retries)
	}
	for _, attempt := range []int{0, 3} {
		if d := backoff(attempt); d != 1500*time.Millisecond {
			t.Fatalf("backoff(%d)=%v, want a fixed 1.5s", attempt, d)
		}
	}
}

// A profile override wins field by field: the pinned count replaces the global
// one, while the interval it left alone still comes from the global policy.
func TestResolveRetryProfileOverridesPerField(t *testing.T) {
	pol := db.LLMRetryPolicy{
		Connect: db.RetryRule{Attempts: 5, IntervalMS: 2000},
		Stream:  db.RetryRule{Attempts: 4, IntervalMS: 1500},
	}
	over := db.RetryOverride{
		Connect: db.RetryRule{Attempts: 1},
		Stream:  db.RetryRule{IntervalMS: 250},
	}
	got := resolveRetry(over, pol)
	if got.ConnectAttempts != 1 || got.ConnectInterval != 2*time.Second {
		t.Fatalf("connect=%d/%v, want 1 attempt inheriting the 2s interval", got.ConnectAttempts, got.ConnectInterval)
	}
	if got.StreamAttempts != 4 || got.StreamInterval != 250*time.Millisecond {
		t.Fatalf("stream=%d/%v, want the global 4 attempts with a pinned 250ms", got.StreamAttempts, got.StreamInterval)
	}
}

// -1 turns the same-provider layer off entirely (0 retries), rather than being
// mistaken for "unset".
func TestSameProviderRetryDisabled(t *testing.T) {
	retries, _ := sameProviderRetryPolicy(agent.RetryConfig{StreamAttempts: -1})
	if retries != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("retries=%d, want 0 (disabled)", retries)
	}
}

// Values beyond the sane range are clamped on the way into the DB, so a hostile
// or fat-fingered payload can't park a worker for a day.
func TestRetryRuleClamp(t *testing.T) {
	pol := db.LLMRetryPolicy{
		Connect: db.RetryRule{Attempts: -50, IntervalMS: -1},
		Stream:  db.RetryRule{Attempts: 9999, IntervalMS: 99_999_999},
	}
	got := resolveRetry(db.RetryOverride{}, pol.Clamped())
	if got.ConnectAttempts != -1 || got.ConnectInterval != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("connect=%d/%v, want -1 attempts and no interval", got.ConnectAttempts, got.ConnectInterval)
	}
	if got.StreamAttempts != 20 || got.StreamInterval != time.Hour {
		t.Fatalf("stream=%d/%v, want the 20-attempt / 1h caps", got.StreamAttempts, got.StreamInterval)
	}
}

FILE: server/login_limit.go

package server

import (
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"net/netip"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// Login attempts are limited per client IP, never per account: a per-account
// lockout would let anyone lock the admin out by failing on purpose.
const (
	loginMaxAttempts = 10               // attempts allowed per IP per window
	loginWindow      = time.Minute      // the counting window
	loginBaseBlock   = time.Minute      // length of the first block
	loginMaxBlock    = 15 * time.Minute // cap on the block; an entry idle this long is dropped
	loginSweepEvery  = time.Minute      // how often stale entries are swept
	loginMaxEntries  = 10000            // hard cap on tracked IPs
)

type loginEntry struct {
	attempts     int
	windowStart  time.Time
	blockedUntil time.Time
	block        time.Duration // current block length; doubles on every new block or blocked attempt
	lastSeen     time.Time
}

// loginLimiter counts login attempts per IP. Past loginMaxAttempts in one
// loginWindow the IP is blocked for loginBaseBlock; every attempt while blocked,
// and every later block, doubles the block up to loginMaxBlock. State is in
// memory only and swept of idle entries, so a restart clears it.
type loginLimiter struct {
	mu        sync.Mutex
	now       func() time.Time
	entries   map[string]*loginEntry
	lastSweep time.Time
}

func newLoginLimiter(now func() time.Time) *loginLimiter {
	return &loginLimiter{now: now, entries: map[string]*loginEntry{}}
}

// allow records one attempt from ip. It returns 0 when the attempt may go on,
// otherwise how long ip must wait.
func (l *loginLimiter) allow(ip string) time.Duration {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	now := l.now()
	l.sweep(now)
	e := l.entries[ip]
	if e == nil {
		if len(l.entries) >= loginMaxEntries {
			l.evictOldest()
		}
		e = &loginEntry{windowStart: now}
		l.entries[ip] = e
	}
	e.lastSeen = now
	if now.Before(e.blockedUntil) {
		e.block = min(2*e.block, loginMaxBlock)
		e.blockedUntil = now.Add(e.block)
		return e.block
	}
	if now.Sub(e.windowStart) >= loginWindow {
		e.attempts, e.windowStart = 0, now
	}
	if e.attempts >= loginMaxAttempts {
		if e.block == 0 {
			e.block = loginBaseBlock
		} else {
			e.block = min(2*e.block, loginMaxBlock)
		}
		e.blockedUntil = now.Add(e.block)
		e.attempts, e.windowStart = 0, now
		return e.block
	}
	e.attempts++
	return 0
}

// reset forgets ip, after a successful login. A blocked IP never reaches the
// password check, so this only runs outside a block.
func (l *loginLimiter) reset(ip string) {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	delete(l.entries, ip)
}

// sweep drops entries idle for loginMaxBlock, at most once per loginSweepEvery.
// Such an entry is never blocked: a block ends at most loginMaxBlock after the
// attempt that set it.
func (l *loginLimiter) sweep(now time.Time) {
	if now.Sub(l.lastSweep) < loginSweepEvery {
		return
	}
	l.lastSweep = now
	for ip, e := range l.entries {
		if now.Sub(e.lastSeen) >= loginMaxBlock {
			delete(l.entries, ip)
		}
	}
}

// evictOldest drops the least recently seen entry to stay under loginMaxEntries.
func (l *loginLimiter) evictOldest() {
	var oldest string
	var at time.Time
	for ip, e := range l.entries {
		if oldest == "" || e.lastSeen.Before(at) {
			oldest, at = ip, e.lastSeen
		}
	}
	delete(l.entries, oldest)
}

// peerIP is the host part of the TCP peer address.
func peerIP(r *http.Request) string {
	host, _, err := net.SplitHostPort(r.RemoteAddr)
	if err != nil {
		return r.RemoteAddr
	}
	return host
}

// clientIP is the address login attempts are counted against. It is the TCP
// peer unless the peer is in trusted: then X-Forwarded-For is read from the
// right, past trusted hops, and the first untrusted hop is the client. Entries
// left of that hop come from the client itself and are never used, so a client
// cannot pick its own bucket. With trusted empty the header is ignored.
func clientIP(r *http.Request, trusted []netip.Prefix) string {
	peer := peerIP(r)
	addr, err := netip.ParseAddr(peer)
	if err != nil || !isTrusted(addr, trusted) {
		return peer
	}
	hops := strings.Split(strings.Join(r.Header.Values("X-Forwarded-For"), ","), ",")
	for i := len(hops) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		hop, err := netip.ParseAddr(strings.TrimSpace(hops[i]))
		if err != nil {
			break // keep the last address a trusted proxy reported
		}
		addr = hop
		if !isTrusted(addr, trusted) {
			break
		}
	}
	return addr.Unmap().WithZone("").String()
}

func isTrusted(a netip.Addr, trusted []netip.Prefix) bool {
	a = a.Unmap().WithZone("")
	for _, p := range trusted {
		if p.Contains(a) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// ParseTrustedProxies parses HIVE_TRUSTED_PROXIES: comma-separated CIDRs (a
// bare address means that one host). Empty means no trusted proxy.
func ParseTrustedProxies(s string) ([]netip.Prefix, error) {
	var out []netip.Prefix
	for _, f := range strings.Split(s, ",") {
		f = strings.TrimSpace(f)
		if f == "" {
			continue
		}
		if p, err := netip.ParsePrefix(f); err == nil {
			out = append(out, p.Masked())
			continue
		}
		a, err := netip.ParseAddr(f)
		if err != nil || a.Zone() != "" {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is not a CIDR or an IP address", f)
		}
		a = a.Unmap()
		out = append(out, netip.PrefixFrom(a, a.BitLen()))
	}
	return out, nil
}

// WithTrustedProxies sets the proxies whose X-Forwarded-For the login rate
// limit reads (see clientIP).
func WithTrustedProxies(p []netip.Prefix) Option {
	return func(s *Server) { s.trustedProxies = p }
}

FILE: server/login_limit_test.go

package server

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"net/netip"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
)

type fakeClock struct{ t time.Time }

func (c *fakeClock) now() time.Time          { return c.t }
func (c *fakeClock) advance(d time.Duration) { c.t = c.t.Add(d) }

func newFakeClock() *fakeClock { return &fakeClock{t: time.Date(2026, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)} }

// oldPassword is 8 characters: valid under the old minimum, too short for a new password now.
const oldPassword = "abcd1234"

// loginServer returns a Server whose login reads a stored hash of oldPassword
// from a stub instead of PostgreSQL.
func loginServer(t *testing.T, clk *fakeClock) (*Server, func(remote, password string, hdr map[string]string) *httptest.ResponseRecorder) {
	t.Helper()
	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(oldPassword), bcrypt.MinCost)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	getSetting := func(key string) (string, bool, error) {
		if key != authPassKey {
			return "", false, nil
		}
		return string(hash), true, nil
	}
	s := &Server{jwtKey: []byte("0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"), loginLimit: newLoginLimiter(clk.now)}
	post := func(remote, password string, hdr map[string]string) *httptest.ResponseRecorder {
		body := fmt.Sprintf(`{"username":"HIVE","password":%q}`, password)
		r := httptest.NewRequest("POST", "/api/auth/login", strings.NewReader(body))
		r.RemoteAddr = remote
		for k, v := range hdr {
			r.Header.Set(k, v)
		}
		w := httptest.NewRecorder()
		s.login(w, r, getSetting)
		return w
	}
	return s, post
}

func failN(t *testing.T, post func(string, string, map[string]string) *httptest.ResponseRecorder, remote string, n int) {
	t.Helper()
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		if w := post(remote, "wrong-password", nil); w.Code != 401 {
			t.Fatalf("attempt %d from %s: status=%d want 401; body=%s", i+1, remote, w.Code, w.Body.String())
		}
	}
}

func TestLoginRateLimitReturns429WithRetryAfter(t *testing.T) {
	clk := newFakeClock()
	_, post := loginServer(t, clk)
	const ip = "192.0.2.10:40000"
	failN(t, post, ip, loginMaxAttempts)

	w := post(ip, oldPassword, nil) // even the right password is refused while blocked
	if w.Code != 429 {
		t.Fatalf("status=%d want 429; body=%s", w.Code, w.Body.String())
	}
	if got := w.Header().Get("Retry-After"); got != "60" {
		t.Fatalf("Retry-After=%q want 60", got)
	}
	var body struct {
		Error string `json:"error"`
		Token string `json:"token"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(w.Body.Bytes(), &body); err != nil || body.Error == "" || body.Token != "" {
		t.Fatalf("want a JSON error body without a token, got %s (err=%v)", w.Body.String(), err)
	}

	// Each attempt while blocked doubles the wait, capped at loginMaxBlock.
	for _, want := range []string{"120", "240", "480", "900", "900"} {
		if got := post(ip, "wrong-password", nil).Header().Get("Retry-After"); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("Retry-After=%q want %s", got, want)
		}
	}

	// Once the block runs out the IP gets a fresh window.
	clk.advance(loginMaxBlock)
	if w := post(ip, oldPassword, nil); w.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("after the block: status=%d want 200; body=%s", w.Code, w.Body.String())
	}
}

func TestLoginSuccessResetsCounter(t *testing.T) {
	clk := newFakeClock()
	_, post := loginServer(t, clk)
	const ip = "192.0.2.11:40000"
	failN(t, post, ip, loginMaxAttempts-1)
	if w := post(ip, oldPassword, nil); w.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("status=%d want 200; body=%s", w.Code, w.Body.String())
	}
	// The counter starts over: a full budget of failures before the next block.
	failN(t, post, ip, loginMaxAttempts)
	if w := post(ip, "wrong-password", nil); w.Code != 429 {
		t.Fatalf("status=%d want 429", w.Code)
	}
}

func TestLoginRateLimitIsPerIP(t *testing.T) {
	clk := newFakeClock()
	_, post := loginServer(t, clk)
	failN(t, post, "192.0.2.12:40000", loginMaxAttempts)
	if w := post("192.0.2.12:40001", "wrong-password", nil); w.Code != 429 {
		t.Fatalf("same IP, other port: status=%d want 429", w.Code)
	}
	if w := post("198.51.100.7:40000", "wrong-password", nil); w.Code != 401 {
		t.Fatalf("other IP: status=%d want 401", w.Code)
	}
	if w := post("[2001:db8::1]:40000", oldPassword, nil); w.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("other IP: status=%d want 200", w.Code)
	}
}

func TestLoginRateLimitIgnoresForwardedFor(t *testing.T) {
	clk := newFakeClock()
	_, post := loginServer(t, clk)
	const blocked = "192.0.2.13"
	failN(t, post, blocked+":40000", loginMaxAttempts)

	// A blocked peer cannot escape by claiming another address.
	for _, h := range []string{"X-Forwarded-For", "X-Real-IP"} {
		if w := post(blocked+":40000", oldPassword, map[string]string{h: "203.0.113.9"}); w.Code != 429 {
			t.Fatalf("%s from blocked peer: status=%d want 429", h, w.Code)
		}
	}
	// And another peer naming the blocked address is not blocked.
	if w := post("198.51.100.8:40000", oldPassword, map[string]string{"X-Forwarded-For": blocked}); w.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("X-Forwarded-For naming the blocked IP: status=%d want 200", w.Code)
	}
}

func mustTrusted(t *testing.T, s string) []netip.Prefix {
	t.Helper()
	p, err := ParseTrustedProxies(s)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return p
}

func TestParseTrustedProxies(t *testing.T) {
	if p, err := ParseTrustedProxies(" "); err != nil || len(p) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("empty: %v, %v; want no proxies", p, err)
	}
	p, err := ParseTrustedProxies(" 127.0.0.1/32, 10.1.2.3/8 ,::1")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := fmt.Sprint(p); got != "[127.0.0.1/32 10.0.0.0/8 ::1/128]" {
		t.Fatalf("got %s", got)
	}
	for _, bad := range []string{"proxy.local", "10.0.0.0/33", "127.0.0.1,nope"} {
		if _, err := ParseTrustedProxies(bad); err == nil {
			t.Fatalf("%q: want an error", bad)
		}
	}
}

func TestClientIP(t *testing.T) {
	trusted := mustTrusted(t, "127.0.0.1/32,10.0.0.0/8")
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name, remote string
		xff          []string
		trusted      []netip.Prefix
		want         string
	}{
		{"direct client, no proxies configured", "198.51.100.9:5000", nil, nil, "198.51.100.9"},
		{"direct client, proxies configured", "198.51.100.9:5000", nil, trusted, "198.51.100.9"},
		{"spoofed header, no proxies configured", "198.51.100.9:5000", []string{"203.0.113.1"}, nil, "198.51.100.9"},
		{"spoofed header from an untrusted peer", "198.51.100.9:5000", []string{"203.0.113.1"}, trusted, "198.51.100.9"},
		{"spoofed header claiming a trusted address", "198.51.100.9:5000", []string{"127.0.0.1"}, trusted, "198.51.100.9"},
		{"one trusted proxy", "127.0.0.1:5000", []string{"198.51.100.7"}, trusted, "198.51.100.7"},
		{"client-supplied entries left of the real hop", "127.0.0.1:5000", []string{"203.0.113.1, 10.0.0.9, 198.51.100.7"}, trusted, "198.51.100.7"},
		{"chain of trusted proxies", "127.0.0.1:5000", []string{"203.0.113.1, 198.51.100.7, 10.0.0.5"}, trusted, "198.51.100.7"},
		{"chain split over header lines", "127.0.0.1:5000", []string{"203.0.113.1", "198.51.100.7, 10.0.0.5"}, trusted, "198.51.100.7"},
		{"trusted proxy without the header", "127.0.0.1:5000", nil, trusted, "127.0.0.1"},
		{"unparsable hop stops the walk", "127.0.0.1:5000", []string{"198.51.100.7, garbage, 10.0.0.5"}, trusted, "10.0.0.5"},
		{"IPv6 client behind the proxy", "127.0.0.1:5000", []string{"2001:db8::7"}, trusted, "2001:db8::7"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			r := httptest.NewRequest("GET", "/", nil)
			r.RemoteAddr = tc.remote
			for _, v := range tc.xff {
				r.Header.Add("X-Forwarded-For", v)
			}
			if got := clientIP(r, tc.trusted); got != tc.want {
				t.Fatalf("clientIP=%s want %s", got, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

// Behind a trusted reverse proxy every request arrives from the proxy's address;
// the limit must still apply per real client.
func TestLoginRateLimitBehindTrustedProxy(t *testing.T) {
	clk := newFakeClock()
	s, post := loginServer(t, clk)
	s.trustedProxies = mustTrusted(t, "127.0.0.1/32")
	const proxy = "127.0.0.1:50000"
	via := func(xff string) map[string]string { return map[string]string{"X-Forwarded-For": xff} }

	for i := 0; i < loginMaxAttempts; i++ {
		if w := post(proxy, "wrong-password", via("198.51.100.20")); w.Code != 401 {
			t.Fatalf("attempt %d: status=%d want 401", i+1, w.Code)
		}
	}
	if w := post(proxy, oldPassword, via("198.51.100.20")); w.Code != 429 {
		t.Fatalf("attacker: status=%d want 429", w.Code)
	}
	// What nginx's $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for sends when the attacker adds its own header.
	if w := post(proxy, oldPassword, via("203.0.113.50, 198.51.100.20")); w.Code != 429 {
		t.Fatalf("attacker with a forged entry: status=%d want 429", w.Code)
	}
	// Another user behind the same proxy is not affected.
	if w := post(proxy, oldPassword, via("198.51.100.21")); w.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("other user via the proxy: status=%d want 200", w.Code)
	}
}

// The 12-character minimum applies to new passwords only. A hash stored under the
// old 8-character minimum must still log in.
func TestEightCharPasswordLogsInButIsRejectedAsNew(t *testing.T) {
	if n := len([]rune(oldPassword)); n != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("oldPassword has %d characters, want 8", n)
	}
	_, post := loginServer(t, newFakeClock())
	w := post("192.0.2.14:40000", oldPassword, nil)
	if w.Code != 200 || !strings.Contains(w.Body.String(), `"token"`) {
		t.Fatalf("login with an existing 8-character password: status=%d body=%s", w.Code, w.Body.String())
	}
	// authInit and authChangePassword both refuse a new password through validatePassword.
	if msg := validatePassword(oldPassword); msg == "" {
		t.Fatal("validatePassword accepted an 8-character new password")
	}
}

func TestLoginLimiterSweepsIdleEntries(t *testing.T) {
	clk := newFakeClock()
	l := newLoginLimiter(clk.now)
	l.allow("192.0.2.20")
	clk.advance(loginMaxBlock - time.Second)
	l.allow("192.0.2.21") // sweeps, but .20 is not idle long enough yet
	if len(l.entries) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("entries=%d want 2 before either is idle for %v", len(l.entries), loginMaxBlock)
	}
	clk.advance(loginSweepEvery)
	l.allow("192.0.2.22") // next sweep drops .20
	if _, ok := l.entries["192.0.2.20"]; ok || len(l.entries) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("idle entry not swept: %d entries", len(l.entries))
	}
}

func TestLoginLimiterCapsEntries(t *testing.T) {
	l := newLoginLimiter(newFakeClock().now)
	for i := 0; i <= loginMaxEntries; i++ {
		l.allow(fmt.Sprintf("10.%d.%d.%d", i>>16&255, i>>8&255, i&255))
	}
	if len(l.entries) != loginMaxEntries {
		t.Fatalf("entries=%d want the cap %d", len(l.entries), loginMaxEntries)
	}
}

func TestHealthHidesVersionWithoutToken(t *testing.T) {
	key := []byte("0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef")
	s := &Server{jwtKey: key}

	w := httptest.NewRecorder()
	s.health(w, httptest.NewRequest("GET", "/api/health", nil))
	if got := strings.TrimSpace(w.Body.String()); w.Code != 200 || got != `{"ok":true}` {
		t.Fatalf("no token: status=%d body=%s want {\"ok\":true}", w.Code, got)
	}

	tok, err := signJWT(key)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	r := httptest.NewRequest("GET", "/api/health", nil)
	r.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+tok)
	w = httptest.NewRecorder()
	s.health(w, r)
	var body map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(w.Body.Bytes(), &body); err != nil || body["version"] != BuildVersion || body["service"] != "hive" {
		t.Fatalf("valid token: body=%s want service and version", w.Body.String())
	}
}

=====================================================================
FILE: server/logsink.go

package server

import (
	"context"
	"io"
	"log"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

// LogLine is one captured backend log entry exposed by the /api/logs endpoints.
type LogLine struct {
	Seq   int64  `json:"seq"`
	DBID  int64  `json:"db_id,omitempty"` // server_logs.id; 0 for pre-persistence entries
	TS    string `json:"ts"`
	Level string `json:"level"` // info | warn | error
	Tag   string `json:"tag"`   // the leading [tag] (pg / planner / activity / …), if any
	Text  string `json:"text"`
}

// dbWriteReq carries a log line to the async DB writer.
type dbWriteReq struct {
	seq int64
	ll  LogLine
}

// logSinkT tees the standard logger into an in-memory ring buffer and fans new
// lines out to SSE subscribers, so the UI can show a live backend log stream.
// It still passes everything through to stderr (the terminal keeps working).
type logSinkT struct {
	mu   sync.Mutex
	ring []LogLine
	cap  int
	seq  int64
	subs map[chan LogLine]struct{}
	out  io.Writer // passthrough (stderr)

	dbOnce sync.Once
	dbCh   chan dbWriteReq // buffered async channel; nil until SetDB is called
}

var logSink = &logSinkT{cap: 3000, subs: map[chan LogLine]struct{}{}, out: os.Stderr}

// StartLogCapture redirects the standard log package through the in-memory sink
// (still writing to stderr). Call once at startup, as early as possible.
func StartLogCapture() { log.SetOutput(logSink) }

// SetDB wires a postgres DB into the sink once (idempotent). It:
//  1. Restores the last 100 log rows from DB into the ring so the /logs page
//     shows history immediately after restart.
//  2. Starts an async goroutine that persists every subsequent log line to DB.
func (s *logSinkT) SetDB(ctx context.Context, pg *db.DB) {
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	s.dbOnce.Do(func() {
		ch := make(chan dbWriteReq, 2000)
		s.mu.Lock()
		s.dbCh = ch
		s.mu.Unlock()

		// Restore last 100 rows from DB → prepend to ring as history context.
		if logs, err := pg.RecentLogs(100); err == nil && len(logs) > 0 {
			s.mu.Lock()
			restored := make([]LogLine, 0, len(logs))
			for _, l := range logs {
				s.seq++
				restored = append(restored, LogLine{
					Seq:   s.seq,
					DBID:  l.ID,
					TS:    l.CreatedAt.Format(time.RFC3339),
					Level: l.Level,
					Tag:   l.Tag,
					Text:  l.Text,
				})
			}
			// Prepend history before any in-memory startup logs already in ring.
			s.ring = append(restored, s.ring...)
			if len(s.ring) > s.cap {
				s.ring = s.ring[len(s.ring)-s.cap:]
			}
			s.mu.Unlock()
		}

		// Async writer: picks from channel and inserts into server_logs.
		// Uses os.Stderr directly to report errors and avoids recursive log calls.
		go func() {
			for {
				select {
				case req, ok := <-ch:
					if !ok {
						return
					}
					id, err := pg.InsertLog(req.ll.Level, req.ll.Tag, req.ll.Text)
					if err != nil {
						_, _ = os.Stderr.Write([]byte("[logsink] db write: " + err.Error() + "\n"))
						continue
					}
					// Stamp DBID back into the ring entry so history pagination works.
					s.mu.Lock()
					for i := range s.ring {
						if s.ring[i].Seq == req.seq {
							s.ring[i].DBID = id
							break
						}
					}
					s.mu.Unlock()
				case <-ctx.Done():
					return
				}
			}
		}()
	})
}

// Write implements io.Writer for the log package: one call per log.Printf line.
func (s *logSinkT) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	_, _ = s.out.Write(p) // keep the terminal output
	line := strings.TrimRight(string(p), "\n")
	if strings.TrimSpace(line) != "" {
		s.add(parseLog(line))
	}
	return len(p), nil
}

func (s *logSinkT) add(l LogLine) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	s.seq++
	l.Seq = s.seq
	s.ring = append(s.ring, l)
	if len(s.ring) > s.cap {
		s.ring = s.ring[len(s.ring)-s.cap:]
	}
	ch := s.dbCh
	subs := make([]chan LogLine, 0, len(s.subs))
	for sub := range s.subs {
		subs = append(subs, sub)
	}
	s.mu.Unlock()

	// Async DB write (non-blocking; drops if channel is full under extreme load).
	if ch != nil {
		select {
		case ch <- dbWriteReq{seq: l.Seq, ll: l}:
		default:
		}
	}

	for _, sub := range subs {
		select {
		case sub <- l:
		default:
		}
	}
}

// recent returns ring lines with Seq > since (capped to limit), and the latest seq.
func (s *logSinkT) recent(since int64, limit int) (lines []LogLine, cursor int64) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	cursor = s.seq
	if limit <= 0 || limit > s.cap {
		limit = s.cap
	}
	for _, l := range s.ring {
		if l.Seq > since {
			lines = append(lines, l)
		}
	}
	if len(lines) > limit {
		lines = lines[len(lines)-limit:]
	}
	return lines, cursor
}

func (s *logSinkT) subscribe() (<-chan LogLine, func()) {
	ch := make(chan LogLine, 256)
	s.mu.Lock()
	s.subs[ch] = struct{}{}
	s.mu.Unlock()
	var once sync.Once
	return ch, func() {
		once.Do(func() {
			s.mu.Lock()
			delete(s.subs, ch)
			s.mu.Unlock()
			close(ch)
		})
	}
}

// parseLog pulls a level + [tag] out of a standard-logger line; the timestamp is
// the capture time (RFC3339).
func parseLog(line string) LogLine {
	msg := line
	// strip the "2006/01/02 15:04:05" LstdFlags prefix if present
	if len(msg) >= 20 && msg[4] == '/' && msg[7] == '/' && msg[10] == ' ' {
		msg = strings.TrimSpace(msg[19:])
	}
	tag := ""
	if strings.HasPrefix(msg, "[") {
		if i := strings.IndexByte(msg, ']'); i > 1 {
			tag = msg[1:i]
		}
	}
	return LogLine{TS: time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339), Level: levelOf(msg), Tag: tag, Text: msg}
}

func levelOf(msg string) string {
	low := strings.ToLower(msg)
	for _, k := range []string{"fatal", "panic", "error", "err:", "failed", "dropped", "refused", "✕", "unreachable"} {
		if strings.Contains(low, k) {
			return "error"
		}
	}
	for _, k := range []string{"warn", "disabled", "disable", "skip", "stopped", "⚠", "retry"} {
		if strings.Contains(low, k) {
			return "warn"
		}
	}
	return "info"
}

package server

import (
	"context"
	"database/sql"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"

	"log"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
