package server

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"iter"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"sync/atomic"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/agent"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/intercept"
	"github.com/Autumn-27/norma/llm"
)

// Target-gate opt-in flag, pins and decisions over the real mux and the real
// auth. The server context is already cancelled, so a task created through
// these tests never starts an engine.

type gateServer struct {
	s     *Server
	m     *Manager
	token string
}

func newGateServer(t *testing.T) *gateServer {
	t.Helper()
	skipWithoutDSN(t)
	m, err := NewManager(t.TempDir(), "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = m.Close() })
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	cancel()
	s := New(ctx, m, t.TempDir(), t.TempDir(), t.TempDir())
	token, err := signJWT(s.jwtKey)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return &gateServer{s: s, m: m, token: token}
}

// do sends an authenticated request. httptest sets the peer to 192.0.2.1.
func (g *gateServer) do(t *testing.T, method, path, body string) (int, map[string]any) {
	t.Helper()
	req := httptest.NewRequest(method, path, strings.NewReader(body))
	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+g.token)
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	g.s.Handler().ServeHTTP(rec, req)
	var out map[string]any
	_ = json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &out)
	return rec.Code, out
}

// newTask creates a task through the manager and removes it, its pins and its
// approval rows when the test ends.
func (g *gateServer) newTask(t *testing.T, opts db.TaskCreateOptions) *Task {
	t.Helper()
	created, err := g.m.CreateTaskWithOptions("target gate flag", "flag, pins and decisions", opts)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	g.cleanupTask(t, created.ID)
	task, ok := g.m.Task(created.ID)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("task not found after creation")
	}
	return task
}

func (g *gateServer) cleanupTask(t *testing.T, id string) {
	t.Helper()
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		n, _ := strconv.ParseInt(id, 10, 64)
		_ = g.m.pg.DeleteTask(n)
		_, _ = g.m.pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM target_pins WHERE task_id=$1`, n)
		_, _ = g.m.pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM intercept_pending WHERE task_id=$1`, id)
	})
}

func taskRef(t *testing.T, task *Task) db.TargetScopeRef {
	t.Helper()
	id, err := strconv.ParseInt(task.ID, 10, 64)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return db.TargetScopeRef{TaskID: id}
}

// openTargetRow opens a target approval request showing ips.
func openTargetRow(t *testing.T, pg *db.DB, scope db.TargetScopeRef, host string, ips ...string) int64 {
	t.Helper()
	id, created, err := pg.FindOrCreateTargetRequest(db.TargetRequest{
		Scope: scope, Host: host, Port: 443, AgentName: "worker", ToolName: "WebFetch", Reason: "target " + host + " is not approved",
		Audit: &db.InterceptAudit{Correlation: "unavailable", InitialAction: "ask", ExecutionStatus: "not_started",
			Targets: []db.InterceptTarget{{Host: host, Port: 443, ResolvedIPs: ips, Resolver: "system", ResolvedAt: time.Now().UTC(), Outcome: "requested"}}},
	})
	if err != nil || !created {
		t.Fatalf("open target request: id=%d created=%v err=%v", id, created, err)
	}
	return id
}

// The flag is read on every tool call: a switch through the API is seen by a
// scope that was handed out before it.
func TestTargetGateLiveSwitch(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	task := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{})
	scope := task.targetScope(intercept.DefaultTargetWaitBound)
	if scope.Enabled == nil || scope.Enabled() {
		t.Fatal("a new task must have the gate off")
	}
	if scope.Interceptor != g.m.interceptor {
		t.Fatal("the task scope does not carry the manager's interceptor")
	}
	if code, body := g.do(t, "GET", "/api/tasks/"+task.ID, ""); code != 200 || body["target_gate"] != false {
		t.Fatalf("task detail: %d %v, want target_gate false", code, body)
	}

	code, body := g.do(t, "PATCH", "/api/tasks/"+task.ID, `{"target_gate":true}`)
	if code != 200 || body["target_gate"] != true {
		t.Fatalf("switch on: %d %v", code, body)
	}
	if !scope.Enabled() {
		t.Fatal("the scope handed out before the switch still reports the gate off")
	}
	id, _ := strconv.ParseInt(task.ID, 10, 64)
	if stored, err := g.m.pg.GetTask(id); err != nil || stored == nil || !stored.TargetGate {
		t.Fatalf("stored task = %+v, %v; want the gate on", stored, err)
	}
	// Another metadata patch leaves the flag alone.
	if code, body := g.do(t, "PATCH", "/api/tasks/"+task.ID, `{"name":"renamed"}`); code != 200 || body["target_gate"] != true || !scope.Enabled() {
		t.Fatalf("rename: %d %v, want the gate still on", code, body)
	}
	if code, body := g.do(t, "PATCH", "/api/tasks/"+task.ID, `{"target_gate":false}`); code != 200 || body["target_gate"] != false || scope.Enabled() {
		t.Fatalf("switch off: %d %v enabled=%v", code, body, scope.Enabled())
	}
	if code, body := g.do(t, "PATCH", "/api/tasks/"+task.ID, `{}`); code != 400 || !strings.Contains(fmt.Sprint(body["error"]), "target_gate") {
		t.Fatalf("empty patch: %d %v, want 400 naming target_gate", code, body)
	}
}

const gateTestGoal = "Probe the lab target at http://127.0.0.1:9/v1 for unauthenticated data exposure; record one record as evidence and stop."

// The flag is set on the existing create path. Omitted means off, and a task
// loaded from the database keeps what was stored.
func TestCreateTaskAcceptsTargetGate(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		field string
		want  bool
	}{
		{`,"target_gate":true`, true},
		{`,"target_gate":false`, false},
		{``, false},
	} {
		code, body := g.do(t, "POST", "/api/tasks", `{"description":"gate create","goal":"`+gateTestGoal+`"`+tc.field+`}`)
		id, _ := body["id"].(string)
		if code != 201 || id == "" {
			t.Fatalf("create %q: %d %v", tc.field, code, body)
		}
		g.cleanupTask(t, id)
		task, ok := g.m.Task(id)
		if !ok || body["target_gate"] != tc.want || task.targetScope(0).Enabled() != tc.want {
			t.Fatalf("create %q: target_gate=%v, want %v", tc.field, body["target_gate"], tc.want)
		}
		n, _ := strconv.ParseInt(id, 10, 64)
		stored, err := g.m.pg.GetTask(n)
		if err != nil || stored == nil || stored.TargetGate != tc.want {
			t.Fatalf("create %q: stored %+v, %v; want %v", tc.field, stored, err, tc.want)
		}
		if loaded := taskFromPG(stored, g.m.pg.Exploration(stored.ExplorationID), g.m.interceptor); loaded.targetScope(0).Enabled() != tc.want {
			t.Fatalf("create %q: a task loaded from the database has the gate %v", tc.field, !tc.want)
		}
	}
}

// ruleLines renders a task's intercept rules for comparison.
func ruleLines(t *testing.T, as *db.AssetStore, taskID string) []string {
	t.Helper()
	n, _ := strconv.ParseInt(taskID, 10, 64)
	rules, err := as.ListTaskInterceptRules(n)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var out []string
	for _, r := range rules {
		out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%s %s %s enabled=%v %q", r.Action, r.Kind, r.Pattern, r.Enabled, r.Note))
	}
	return out
}

// checkSpawnedChild checks the target-gate state of a spawned task: the flag,
// live and stored, no pin, and its own intercept rules.
func (g *gateServer) checkSpawnedChild(t *testing.T, childID string, gate bool, rules []string) {
	t.Helper()
	child, ok := g.m.Task(childID)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("spawned task %s not found", childID)
	}
	if child.targetScope(0).Enabled() != gate {
		t.Fatalf("spawned task gate = %v, want %v", !gate, gate)
	}
	n, _ := strconv.ParseInt(childID, 10, 64)
	if stored, err := g.m.pg.GetTask(n); err != nil || stored == nil || stored.TargetGate != gate {
		t.Fatalf("stored child = %+v, %v; want the gate %v", stored, err, gate)
	}
	if pins, err := g.m.pg.ListTargetPins(db.TargetScopeRef{TaskID: n}); err != nil || len(pins) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("the spawned task has pins: %+v, %v", pins, err)
	}
	if got := ruleLines(t, g.m.Assets(), childID); !slices.Equal(got, rules) {
		t.Fatalf("spawned task rules = %q, want %q", got, rules)
	}
}

// A task spawned through spawn_task takes the target gate of the calling scope
// (D23) and, from a gated task, that task's block rules (D24). It never takes
// pins or allow rules, and parent_ref plays no part. A gate-off caller and a
// call with no scope create the child as before: gate off, no rules.
func TestSpawnedTaskInheritsGateFromCaller(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	on := true
	parentRules := []db.TaskInterceptRuleInput{
		{Enabled: true, Action: "block", Kind: "exact_domain", Pattern: "blocked.example.com", Note: "out of scope"},
		{Enabled: false, Action: "block", Kind: "cidr", Pattern: "198.51.100.0/24"},
		{Enabled: true, Action: "allow", Kind: "exact_domain", Pattern: "allowed.example.com"},
	}
	gated := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{TargetGate: &on, InterceptRules: parentRules})
	open := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{InterceptRules: parentRules})
	if !gated.targetScope(0).Enabled() || open.targetScope(0).Enabled() {
		t.Fatal("control: one parent gated, the other not")
	}
	// The gated parent holds one pin, which no child may get.
	if p, ok, err := g.m.pg.ResolveTargetRequest(openTargetRow(t, g.m.pg, taskRef(t, gated), "app.example.com", "203.0.113.7"), true, "HIVE", "192.0.2.1"); err != nil || !ok || p == nil {
		t.Fatalf("pin the parent: %+v ok=%v err=%v", p, ok, err)
	}
	conv, err := g.m.pg.CreateConversationGated("auto", "spawn from a gated chat", nil, true)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = g.m.pg.DeleteConversation(conv.ID) })
	gatedChat := intercept.TargetScope{ConversationID: conv.ID, Enabled: func() bool { return true },
		WaitBound: intercept.DefaultTargetWaitBound, Interceptor: g.m.interceptor}
	scoped := func(s intercept.TargetScope) context.Context {
		return intercept.WithTargetScope(context.Background(), s)
	}
	blockOnly := []string{
		`block exact_domain blocked.example.com enabled=true "out of scope"`,
		`block cidr 198.51.100.0/24 enabled=false ""`,
	}

	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name      string
		ctx       context.Context
		parentRef string
		gate      bool
		rules     []string
	}{
		{"gated task", scoped(gated.targetScope(intercept.DefaultTargetWaitBound)), "", true, blockOnly},
		{"gated task, parent_ref names a gate-off task", scoped(gated.targetScope(0)), open.ID, true, blockOnly},
		{"gated conversation", scoped(gatedChat), "", true, nil},
		{"gate-off task", scoped(open.targetScope(0)), "", false, nil},
		{"gate-off task, parent_ref names a gated task", scoped(open.targetScope(0)), gated.ID, false, nil},
		{"no scope, parent_ref names a gated task", context.Background(), gated.ID, false, nil},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			args := map[string]any{"description": "spawned child", "goal": gateTestGoal}
			if tc.parentRef != "" {
				args["parent_ref"] = tc.parentRef
			}
			in, _ := json.Marshal(args)
			res, err := g.s.toolSpawnTask().Call(tc.ctx, in, nil)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			childID, found := strings.CutPrefix(res.Flatten(), "task created: ")
			if !found {
				t.Fatalf("spawn_task result: %q", res.Flatten())
			}
			g.cleanupTask(t, childID)
			if child, _ := g.m.Task(childID); child == nil || child.ParentRef != tc.parentRef {
				t.Fatalf("spawned task = %+v, want parent_ref %q", child, tc.parentRef)
			}
			g.checkSpawnedChild(t, childID, tc.gate, tc.rules)
		})
	}
	// The callers are unchanged.
	if pins, err := g.m.pg.ListTargetPins(taskRef(t, gated)); err != nil || len(pins) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("parent pins = %+v, %v; want still one", pins, err)
	}
	if got := ruleLines(t, g.m.Assets(), gated.ID); len(got) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("parent rules = %q, want the three it was created with", got)
	}
}

// toolCallProvider is a model that makes one tool call on its first turn and
// ends the run on the next.
type toolCallProvider struct {
	tool, input string
	turn        atomic.Int64
}

func (p *toolCallProvider) Stream(context.Context, llm.CompletionRequest) iter.Seq2[llm.StreamEvent, error] {
	events := []llm.StreamEvent{{Type: llm.SETextDelta, Text: "done"}, {Type: llm.SEMessageDelta, StopReason: "end_turn"}}
	if p.turn.Add(1) == 1 {
		events = []llm.StreamEvent{
			{Type: llm.SEToolUseStart, ToolID: "call-1", ToolName: p.tool},
			{Type: llm.SEToolInputJSON, Text: p.input},
			{Type: llm.SEMessageDelta, StopReason: "tool_use"},
		}
	}
	return func(yield func(llm.StreamEvent, error) bool) {
		for _, event := range events {
			if !yield(event, nil) {
				return
			}
		}
	}
}

func (p *toolCallProvider) Complete(ctx context.Context, req llm.CompletionRequest) (llm.Message, string, llm.Usage, error) {
	return accumulateStreamForTest(ctx, p.Stream, req)
}

// spawn_task called by the model of an auto conversation, through the real
// harness, tool binding and tool context: the child takes the conversation's
// flag. The unit test above builds the caller's context by hand; this one shows
// the conversation's scope reaches the tool.
func TestSpawnTaskSeesCallerScopeThroughHarness(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	for _, gate := range []bool{true, false} {
		t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("conversation gate %v", gate), func(t *testing.T) {
			desc := fmt.Sprintf("harness child %v %d", gate, time.Now().UnixNano())
			in, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"description": desc, "goal": gateTestGoal})
			conv, err := g.m.pg.CreateConversationGated("auto", "spawn through the harness", nil, gate)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			t.Cleanup(func() { _ = g.m.pg.DeleteConversation(conv.ID) })
			g.s.cfgMu.Lock()
			g.s.chatAgent = agent.NewChatAgent(&toolCallProvider{tool: "spawn_task", input: string(in)}, "test-model", g.m.dir, nil, 10000)
			g.s.cfgMu.Unlock()
			// The server context of this fixture is cancelled; the turn gets its own.
			ctx, cancel := context.WithCancelCause(intercept.WithConvID(context.Background(), conv.ID))
			g.s.runConversationTurn(ctx, cancel, conv, "spawn the child task", g.s.convBusyKey(conv.ID))
			var childID string
			for _, task := range g.m.List() {
				if task.Description == desc {
					childID = task.ID
				}
			}
			if childID == "" {
				t.Fatal("the model's spawn_task call created no task")
			}
			g.cleanupTask(t, childID)
			g.checkSpawnedChild(t, childID, gate, nil)
		})
	}
}

// A conversation started by a trigger of a gated task is gated (D25): a single
// fire, a by-task merge, and a merge across tasks of which one is gated. A fire
// of a gate-off task, or with no task, starts it gate off as before. The flag is
// copied, never pins.
func TestTriggeredConversationInheritsGate(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	g.s.cfgMu.Lock()
	g.s.chatAgent = agent.NewChatAgent(newScopeProbeProvider(), "test-model", g.m.dir, nil, 10000)
	g.s.cfgMu.Unlock()
	on := true
	gated, open := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{TargetGate: &on}), g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{})
	if p, ok, err := g.m.pg.ResolveTargetRequest(openTargetRow(t, g.m.pg, taskRef(t, gated), "app.example.com", "203.0.113.7"), true, "HIVE", "192.0.2.1"); err != nil || !ok || p == nil {
		t.Fatalf("pin the gated task: %+v ok=%v err=%v", p, ok, err)
	}
	gatedID, openID := taskRef(t, gated).TaskID, taskRef(t, open).TaskID

	// The server context is cancelled, so StartTriggeredRun only queues. The test
	// takes the next run with the merge mode under test and runs it as the pump would.
	trigger := func(t *testing.T, mode string, taskIDs ...int64) *db.Conversation {
		t.Helper()
		key := fmt.Sprintf("gate-trigger-%d", time.Now().UnixNano())
		for _, id := range taskIDs {
			g.s.StartTriggeredRun(key, "trigger", "event body", id, id > 0, "desc", "goal")
		}
		g.s.queueMu.Lock()
		item := g.s.nextTriggerRun(key, triggerBehavior{runMode: "serial", mergeMode: mode})
		left := len(g.s.triggerQ[key])
		delete(g.s.triggerQ, key)
		delete(g.s.triggerCfg, key)
		g.s.queueMu.Unlock()
		if left != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("%d fires left in the queue, want one run", left)
		}
		item.title = key
		g.s.runTriggeredRun(item)
		convs, err := g.m.pg.ListConversations()
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		for _, c := range convs {
			if c.Title == key {
				t.Cleanup(func() { _ = g.m.pg.DeleteConversation(c.ID) })
				return c
			}
		}
		t.Fatal("the trigger created no conversation")
		return nil
	}

	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name  string
		mode  string
		tasks []int64
		gate  bool
	}{
		{"gated task", "none", []int64{gatedID}, true},
		{"gated task, merged by task", "by_task", []int64{gatedID, gatedID}, true},
		{"merge across tasks, gated second", "all", []int64{openID, gatedID}, true},
		{"gate-off task", "none", []int64{openID}, false},
		{"gate-off task, merged by task", "by_task", []int64{openID, openID}, false},
		{"no task", "none", []int64{0}, false},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			c := trigger(t, tc.mode, tc.tasks...)
			if c.TargetGate != tc.gate {
				t.Fatalf("triggered conversation gate = %v, want %v", c.TargetGate, tc.gate)
			}
			if pins, err := g.m.pg.ListTargetPins(db.TargetScopeRef{ConversationID: c.ID}); err != nil || len(pins) != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("the triggered conversation has pins: %+v, %v", pins, err)
			}
		})
	}
}

// The conversation flag is set on create and on patch, and the turn that starts
// after a switch runs with the new value.
func TestConversationTargetGateOverHTTP(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	turnScope := func(id int64) intercept.TargetScope {
		t.Helper()
		conv, err := g.m.pg.GetConversation(id)
		if err != nil || conv == nil {
			t.Fatalf("conversation %d: %+v, %v", id, conv, err)
		}
		probe := newScopeProbeProvider()
		g.s.cfgMu.Lock()
		g.s.chatAgent = agent.NewChatAgent(probe, "test-model", g.m.dir, nil, 10000)
		g.s.cfgMu.Unlock()
		// The server context of this fixture is cancelled; the turn gets its own.
		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancelCause(intercept.WithConvID(context.Background(), id))
		g.s.runConversationTurn(ctx, cancel, conv, "hello", g.s.convBusyKey(id))
		got := probe.first(t)
		if !got.ok || got.scope.ConversationID != id || got.scope.Enabled == nil {
			t.Fatalf("turn scope = %+v (present=%v)", got.scope, got.ok)
		}
		return got.scope
	}
	create := func(body string) int64 {
		t.Helper()
		code, out := g.do(t, "POST", "/api/conversations", body)
		id, _ := out["id"].(float64)
		if code != 200 || id == 0 {
			t.Fatalf("create conversation: %d %v", code, out)
		}
		t.Cleanup(func() { _ = g.m.pg.DeleteConversation(int64(id)) })
		return int64(id)
	}

	plain := create(`{"agent_key":"auto","title":"gate off"}`)
	if scope := turnScope(plain); scope.Enabled() {
		t.Fatal("a conversation created without the flag runs with the gate on")
	}
	gated := create(`{"agent_key":"auto","title":"gate on","target_gate":true}`)
	scope := turnScope(gated)
	if !scope.Enabled() || scope.Interceptor != g.m.interceptor {
		t.Fatalf("gated conversation: enabled=%v, want the gate on and the manager's interceptor", scope.Enabled())
	}
	path := "/api/conversations/" + strconv.FormatInt(gated, 10)
	if code, out := g.do(t, "PATCH", path, `{"target_gate":false}`); code != 200 || out["target_gate"] != false {
		t.Fatalf("switch off: %d %v", code, out)
	}
	if turnScope(gated).Enabled() {
		t.Fatal("the turn after the switch still runs with the gate on")
	}
	if code, out := g.do(t, "PATCH", path, `{"title":"renamed","target_gate":true}`); code != 200 || out["target_gate"] != true || out["title"] != "renamed" {
		t.Fatalf("switch on with a rename: %d %v", code, out)
	}
	if code, out := g.do(t, "PATCH", path, `{}`); code != 400 || !strings.Contains(fmt.Sprint(out["error"]), "target_gate") {
		t.Fatalf("empty patch: %d %v, want 400 naming target_gate", code, out)
	}
}

// The decide endpoint keeps its request and response shape. On a target row
// "allowed" pins the displayed addresses. Every human decision, on a target row
// or on a classic ask, records the subject of the session token and the remote
// address; decided_by stays the actor class.
func TestInterceptDecideRecordsApproverOverHTTP(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	task := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{})
	scope := taskRef(t, task)
	pg := g.m.pg
	decide := func(id int64, decision string) int {
		t.Helper()
		code, _ := g.do(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/api/intercept/pending/%d/decide", id), `{"decision":"`+decision+`"}`)
		return code
	}

	target := openTargetRow(t, pg, scope, "app.example.com", "203.0.113.7")
	if code := decide(target, "allowed"); code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("decide target row: %d", code)
	}
	pins, err := pg.ListTargetPins(scope)
	if err != nil || len(pins) != 1 || pins[0].DecidedBy != "HIVE" || pins[0].DecidedFrom != "192.0.2.1" ||
		!slices.Equal(pins[0].PinnedIPs, []string{"203.0.113.7"}) || pins[0].InterceptID == nil || *pins[0].InterceptID != target {
		t.Fatalf("pins = %+v, %v; want one pin with the approver and the address", pins, err)
	}
	row, err := pg.GetInterceptDetail(target)
	if err != nil || row == nil || row.Status != "allowed" || row.DecidedBy != "human" || row.Audit.Approver != "HIVE" || row.Audit.ApproverAddr != "192.0.2.1" {
		t.Fatalf("target row = %+v, %v", row, err)
	}
	if code := decide(target, "denied"); code != 409 {
		t.Fatalf("second decision: %d, want 409", code)
	}

	denied := openTargetRow(t, pg, scope, "other.example.com", "203.0.113.8")
	if code := decide(denied, "denied"); code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("deny target row: %d", code)
	}
	if pins, err := pg.ListTargetPins(scope); err != nil || len(pins) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("pins after a denial = %+v, %v; want still one", pins, err)
	}

	classic, err := pg.CreateInterceptPending(0, 0, task.ID, "worker", "Bash", []byte(`{"command":"id"}`), "classic ask",
		&db.InterceptAudit{Correlation: "exact", InitialAction: "ask", ExecutionStatus: "not_started"})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if code := decide(classic, "allowed"); code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("decide classic ask: %d", code)
	}
	row, err = pg.GetInterceptDetail(classic)
	if err != nil || row == nil || row.Status != "allowed" || row.DecidedBy != "human" || row.Audit == nil ||
		row.Audit.Approver != "HIVE" || row.Audit.ApproverAddr != "192.0.2.1" || row.Audit.EffectiveAction != "allow" {
		t.Fatalf("classic row = %+v, %v; want the approver and the address in its audit", row, err)
	}
	if pins, err := pg.ListTargetPins(scope); err != nil || len(pins) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("pins after a classic approval = %+v, %v; want still one", pins, err)
	}

	// Target rows are listed under their own decision source.
	code, list := g.do(t, "GET", "/api/intercept/task/"+task.ID+"?decision_source=target&page=1&size=50", "")
	if items, _ := list["items"].([]any); code != 200 || len(items) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("decision_source=target: %d %v, want the two target rows", code, list)
	}
	if code, _ := g.do(t, "GET", "/api/intercept/history?decision_source=nonsense&page=1", ""); code != 400 {
		t.Fatalf("unknown decision_source: %d, want 400", code)
	}
}

func TestJWTSubject(t *testing.T) {
	key := []byte("0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef")
	token, err := signJWT(key)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := jwtSubject(token, key); got != "HIVE" {
		t.Fatalf("subject = %q, want HIVE", got)
	}
	if got := jwtSubject(token, []byte("another key, another key, another")); got != "" {
		t.Fatalf("subject of a token signed with another key = %q, want none", got)
	}
	if got := jwtSubject("", key); got != "" {
		t.Fatalf("subject of no token = %q", got)
	}
}

// Pin routes: list and revoke, scoped to one existing task or conversation.
func TestTargetPinRoutes(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	pg := g.m.pg
	task, other := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{}), g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{})
	conv, err := pg.CreateConversation("auto", "pin routes", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		_ = pg.DeleteConversation(conv.ID)
		_, _ = pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM target_pins WHERE conversation_id=$1`, conv.ID)
	})
	pin := func(scope db.TargetScopeRef, host string) int64 {
		t.Helper()
		p, ok, err := pg.ResolveTargetRequest(openTargetRow(t, pg, scope, host, "203.0.113.7"), true, "HIVE", "192.0.2.1")
		if err != nil || !ok || p == nil {
			t.Fatalf("pin %s: %+v ok=%v err=%v", host, p, ok, err)
		}
		return p.ID
	}
	taskPin := pin(taskRef(t, task), "app.example.com")
	otherPin := pin(taskRef(t, other), "app.example.com")
	convPin := pin(db.TargetScopeRef{ConversationID: conv.ID}, "chat.example.com")

	listed := func(path string) []any {
		t.Helper()
		code, body := g.do(t, "GET", path, "")
		pins, ok := body["pins"].([]any)
		if code != 200 || !ok {
			t.Fatalf("GET %s: %d %v", path, code, body)
		}
		return pins
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		base string
		id   int64
		host string
	}{
		{"/api/tasks/" + task.ID, taskPin, "app.example.com"},
		{"/api/conversations/" + strconv.FormatInt(conv.ID, 10), convPin, "chat.example.com"},
	} {
		pins := listed(tc.base + "/target-pins")
		if len(pins) != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("%s: %d pins, want 1", tc.base, len(pins))
		}
		got := pins[0].(map[string]any)
		if got["id"] != float64(tc.id) || got["host"] != tc.host || got["status"] != "active" || got["decided_by"] != "HIVE" || got["name_only_effective"] != false {
			t.Fatalf("%s: listed pin = %v", tc.base, got)
		}
		revoke := fmt.Sprintf("%s/target-pins/%d/revoke", tc.base, tc.id)
		code, body := g.do(t, "POST", revoke, "")
		if code != 200 || body["status"] != "revoked" || body["revoked_reason"] != "operator" {
			t.Fatalf("POST %s: %d %v", revoke, code, body)
		}
		at := body["revoked_at"]
		// Revoking again changes nothing.
		if code, body := g.do(t, "POST", revoke, ""); code != 200 || body["status"] != "revoked" || body["revoked_at"] != at {
			t.Fatalf("second POST %s: %d %v", revoke, code, body)
		}
		if pins := listed(tc.base + "/target-pins"); len(pins) != 1 || pins[0].(map[string]any)["status"] != "revoked" {
			t.Fatalf("%s after the revoke: %v, want the pin kept as revoked", tc.base, pins)
		}
		// A pin of another scope is not reachable through this one.
		if code, _ := g.do(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("%s/target-pins/%d/revoke", tc.base, otherPin), ""); code != 404 {
			t.Fatalf("revoke of a foreign pin through %s: %d, want 404", tc.base, code)
		}
	}
	if active, err := pg.ActiveTargetPins(taskRef(t, other), "app.example.com", 443); err != nil || len(active) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("the pin of the other task = %+v, %v; want still active", active, err)
	}
	for _, path := range []string{"/api/tasks/999999999/target-pins", "/api/conversations/999999999/target-pins"} {
		if code, _ := g.do(t, "GET", path, ""); code != 404 {
			t.Fatalf("GET %s: %d, want 404", path, code)
		}
	}
	if code, _ := g.do(t, "POST", "/api/tasks/"+task.ID+"/target-pins/notanumber/revoke", ""); code != 400 {
		t.Fatalf("revoke with a bad pin id: %d, want 400", code)
	}
}

// A worker that loses its claim while it waits in the gate stops waiting, and
// the request stays open: it is host-level, not owned by the call. The worker
// that took the intent over attaches to the same request.
func TestClaimLostEndsGateWait(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	task := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{})
	pg, ic := g.m.pg, g.m.interceptor
	store := task.Store
	intent, err := store.AddIntent(map[string]any{"summary": "leased"}, 1, nil, "planner")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	token, err := store.ClaimIntentToken(intent, "work#1")
	if err != nil || token == "" {
		t.Fatalf("claim: token=%q err=%v", token, err)
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancelCause(intercept.WithTaskContext(context.Background(), task.ID, "work#1", nil))
	defer cancel(nil)
	stop := startClaimHeartbeat(store, 20*time.Millisecond, "work#1", intent, token, cancel)
	defer stop()

	scope := task.targetScope(time.Minute)
	targets := []intercept.TargetRequest{{Host: "app.example.com", Port: 443, ResolvedIPs: []string{"203.0.113.7"}, Resolver: "system", ResolvedAt: time.Now().UTC(), Reason: "no_pin"}}
	input := []byte(`{"url":"https://app.example.com/"}`)
	stale := make(chan intercept.TargetResult, 1)
	go func() { stale <- ic.RequestTargets(ctx, scope, "WebFetch", input, targets, nil) }()
	openRows := func() []int64 {
		t.Helper()
		rows, err := pg.Query(`SELECT id FROM intercept_pending WHERE task_id=$1 AND status='pending' AND target_key IS NOT NULL ORDER BY id`, task.ID)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		defer rows.Close()
		var ids []int64
		for rows.Next() {
			var id int64
			if err := rows.Scan(&id); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			ids = append(ids, id)
		}
		return ids
	}
	waitUntil(t, "the gate request", func() bool { return len(openRows()) == 1 })
	request := openRows()[0]
	select {
	case res := <-stale:
		t.Fatalf("the call returned %+v while its claim was live", res)
	case <-time.After(200 * time.Millisecond):
	}

	// Takeover, as in TestClaimHeartbeatRenewsThenCancelsOnTakeover.
	var reclaimed int64
	for attempt := 0; attempt < 200 && reclaimed == 0; attempt++ {
		if _, err := pg.Exec(`UPDATE exploration_nodes SET last_heartbeat_at = now() - $2 * INTERVAL '1 second' WHERE id=$1`,
			intent, (db.IntentClaimTTL + time.Second).Seconds()); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if reclaimed, err = store.ResetRunningIntents(); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	if reclaimed != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("could not take the claim over: reclaimed=%d", reclaimed)
	}
	if other, err := store.ClaimIntentToken(intent, "work#2"); err != nil || other == "" {
		t.Fatalf("re-claim: token=%q err=%v", other, err)
	}

	var res intercept.TargetResult
	select {
	case res = <-stale:
	case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the gate wait did not end after the claim was lost")
	}
	if cause := context.Cause(ctx); !errors.Is(cause, agent.AbortWorkClaimLost) {
		t.Fatalf("cancel cause=%v, want AbortWorkClaimLost", cause)
	}
	if res.Code != intercept.TargetApprovalPending || res.PendingID != request {
		t.Fatalf("stale call: %+v, want %s on request %d", res, intercept.TargetApprovalPending, request)
	}
	if row, err := pg.GetInterceptPending(request); err != nil || row == nil || row.Status != "pending" || row.DecidedBy != "" {
		t.Fatalf("request after the claim was lost = %+v, %v; want still open", row, err)
	}

	// The second claimer re-runs the intent, hits the same host and attaches.
	next := make(chan intercept.TargetResult, 1)
	go func() {
		next <- ic.RequestTargets(intercept.WithTaskContext(context.Background(), task.ID, "work#2", nil), scope, "WebFetch", input, targets, nil)
	}()
	select {
	case res := <-next:
		t.Fatalf("the second claimer returned %+v before a decision", res)
	case <-time.After(200 * time.Millisecond):
	}
	if ids := openRows(); !slices.Equal(ids, []int64{request}) {
		t.Fatalf("open requests = %v, want the second claimer on the same request %d", ids, request)
	}
	if err := ic.Decide(request, true, "HIVE", "192.0.2.1"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	select {
	case res := <-next:
		if res.Code != "" {
			t.Fatalf("second claimer after the approval: %+v", res)
		}
	case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the second claimer is still waiting after the approval")
	}
	if pins, err := pg.ListTargetPins(taskRef(t, task)); err != nil || len(pins) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("pins = %+v, %v; want one", pins, err)
	}
}

package server

import (
	"context"
	"iter"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"sync/atomic"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/agent"

// Target-gate wiring: every platform-owned session starts on a context that
// carries the approval scope of its task or conversation, and the planner and
// the main agent run with the task's target-only hooks. The gate is off, so
// none of this changes what a session does.

// innerHooksProbe is a programmable inner HookRunner that records what
// steerHooks hands it.
type innerHooksProbe struct {
	block   bool
	msg     string
	updated []byte

	pre, post int
	tool      string
	input     string
	scoped    bool
}

func (p *innerHooksProbe) PreToolUse(ctx context.Context, name string, input []byte) (bool, string, []byte) {
	p.pre++
	p.tool, p.input = name, string(input)
	_, p.scoped = intercept.TargetScopeFromContext(ctx)
	return p.block, p.msg, p.updated
}

func (p *innerHooksProbe) PostToolUse(context.Context, string, []byte, []byte, bool) { p.post++ }

func (p *innerHooksProbe) Stop(context.Context, []llm.Message) (bool, []string, string) {
	return false, nil, ""
}

// The worker's hooks are the task Guard wrapped in steerHooks. The wrapper must
// hand the call, on the caller's context, to the inner hooks and return their
// decision unchanged — a block decided by the Guard must not be lost on the way.
func TestSteerHooksForwardInnerBlock(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := intercept.WithTargetScope(context.Background(), intercept.TargetScope{TaskID: "7"})
	noSteer := func() (string, bool) { return "", false }
	input := []byte(`{"command":"curl https://app.example.com/"}`)

	inner := &innerHooksProbe{block: true, msg: "inner refused"}
	h := steerHooks{inner: inner, drain: noSteer, nudges: &atomic.Int64{}}
	block, msg, updated := h.PreToolUse(ctx, "Bash", input)
	if !block || msg != "inner refused" || updated != nil {
		t.Fatalf("inner block not forwarded: block=%v msg=%q updated=%q", block, msg, updated)
	}
	if inner.pre != 1 || inner.tool != "Bash" || inner.input != string(input) || !inner.scoped {
		t.Fatalf("inner hooks saw pre=%d tool=%q input=%q scoped=%v", inner.pre, inner.tool, inner.input, inner.scoped)
	}

	// An inner pass (with a rewritten input) is forwarded just the same.
	inner = &innerHooksProbe{updated: []byte(`{"command":"true"}`)}
	h = steerHooks{inner: inner, drain: noSteer, nudges: &atomic.Int64{}}
	if block, msg, updated := h.PreToolUse(ctx, "Bash", input); block || msg != "" || string(updated) != `{"command":"true"}` {
		t.Fatalf("inner pass not forwarded: block=%v msg=%q updated=%q", block, msg, updated)
	}
	h.PostToolUse(ctx, "Bash", input, []byte(`"ok"`), false)
	if inner.post != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("PostToolUse reached the inner hooks %d times, want 1", inner.post)
	}

	// A queued steer message is delivered first; the inner hooks are not asked.
	inner = &innerHooksProbe{}
	h = steerHooks{inner: inner, drain: func() (string, bool) { return "change course", true }, nudges: &atomic.Int64{}}
	if block, msg, _ := h.PreToolUse(ctx, "Bash", input); !block || !strings.Contains(msg, "change course") || inner.pre != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("steer message: block=%v msg=%q inner.pre=%d", block, msg, inner.pre)
	}
}

// scopeProbe is the target scope a session's context carried.
type scopeProbe struct {
	scope intercept.TargetScope
	ok    bool
}

// scopeProbeProvider is a model that lists its work dir (a read-only LS call) on
// its first turn and ends the run on the next, recording the target scope of the
// context it is called with. The harness calls the model and the tool hooks on
// the same session context.
type scopeProbeProvider struct {
	seen chan scopeProbe
	turn atomic.Int64
}

func newScopeProbeProvider() *scopeProbeProvider {
	return &scopeProbeProvider{seen: make(chan scopeProbe, 16)}
}

func (p *scopeProbeProvider) Stream(ctx context.Context, _ llm.CompletionRequest) iter.Seq2[llm.StreamEvent, error] {
	scope, ok := intercept.TargetScopeFromContext(ctx)
	select {
	case p.seen <- scopeProbe{scope, ok}:
	default:
	}
	events := []llm.StreamEvent{{Type: llm.SETextDelta, Text: "done"}, {Type: llm.SEMessageDelta, StopReason: "end_turn"}}
	if p.turn.Add(1) == 1 {
		events = []llm.StreamEvent{
			{Type: llm.SEToolUseStart, ToolID: "call-1", ToolName: "LS"},
			{Type: llm.SEToolInputJSON, Text: `{}`},
			{Type: llm.SEMessageDelta, StopReason: "tool_use"},
		}
	}
	return func(yield func(llm.StreamEvent, error) bool) {
		for _, event := range events {
			if !yield(event, nil) {
				return
			}
		}
	}
}

func (p *scopeProbeProvider) Complete(ctx context.Context, req llm.CompletionRequest) (llm.Message, string, llm.Usage, error) {
	return accumulateStreamForTest(ctx, p.Stream, req)
}

// first returns the scope of the first model call, failing if none arrives.
func (p *scopeProbeProvider) first(t *testing.T) scopeProbe {
	t.Helper()
	select {
	case s := <-p.seen:
		return s
	case <-time.After(30 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the session never called the model")
		return scopeProbe{}
	}
}

// targetScopeFixture is a manager, engine and server on the test database.

}

		t.Fatal(err)
	}

// newTask creates a task with one open goal (so the planner loop plans).
func (f *targetScopeFixture) newTask(t *testing.T) *Task {
	t.Helper()

	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	task, ok := f.m.Task(created.ID)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("task not found after creation")
	}
	if _, err := task.Store.AddGoal(map[string]any{"summary": "probe goal"}, "seed"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

// usePlanner makes the engine resolve every task to agents driven by p.
func (f *targetScopeFixture) usePlanner(p llm.Provider) {
	planner := agent.NewPlanner(p, "test-model", f.m.dir, nil, 0, 3)
	worker := agent.NewWorker(p, "test-model", f.m.dir, nil, 0, 3)
	f.e.SetAuthoritativeAgentResolver(func(*Task) (*agent.Planner, *agent.Worker) { return planner, worker })
}

// waitUntil polls cond until it holds, failing after 30 seconds.
func waitUntil(t *testing.T, what string, cond func() bool) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(30 * time.Second)
	for !cond() {
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s", what)
		}
		time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}

// plannerLoopRound runs the planner loop until its first round has finished and
// returns the scope that round's session carried.
func (f *targetScopeFixture) plannerLoopRound(t *testing.T, task *Task) scopeProbe {
	t.Helper()
	probe := newScopeProbeProvider()
	f.usePlanner(probe)
	ctx, stop := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(done)
		f.e.plannerLoop(ctx, task)
	}()
	task.Notify()
	got := probe.first(t)
	waitUntil(t, "the planning round to finish", func() bool { return f.e.inflightCount(task.ID) == 0 })
	stop()
	<-done
	return got
}

// finalPlannerRound runs the task-timeout settlement round and returns the scope
// its session carried.
func (f *targetScopeFixture) finalPlannerRound(t *testing.T, task *Task) scopeProbe {
	t.Helper()
	probe := newScopeProbeProvider()
	f.usePlanner(probe)
	f.e.runFinalPlannerRound(context.Background(), task, false)
	return probe.first(t)
}

func (f *targetScopeFixture) mainAgentTurn(t *testing.T, task *Task) scopeProbe {
	t.Helper()
	probe := newScopeProbeProvider()
	f.s.cfgMu.Lock()
	f.s.llmOn, f.s.llmProv = true, probe
	f.s.cfgMu.Unlock()
	f.s.taskAgentMu.Lock()
	f.s.taskAgents[task.ID] = &taskAgentBundle{main: agent.NewMainAgent(probe, "test-model", f.m.dir, nil, 0, 3)}
	f.s.taskAgentMu.Unlock()
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	f.s.chat(rec, httptest.NewRequest("POST", "/api/chat?task="+task.ID, strings.NewReader(`{"message":"status?"}`)))
	if rec.Code != 202 {
		t.Fatalf("chat status = %d, want 202: %s", rec.Code, rec.Body.String())
	}
	got := probe.first(t)
	waitUntil(t, "the main-agent turn to finish", func() bool {
		f.s.chatMu.Lock()
		defer f.s.chatMu.Unlock()
		return !f.s.chatBusy[task.ID]
	})
	return got
}

func (f *targetScopeFixture) workerIntent(t *testing.T, task *Task) scopeProbe {

	if _, err := task.Store.AddIntent(map[string]any{"summary": "scope probe"}, 1, nil, "planner"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	if intent == nil {
		t.Fatal("no intent claimed")
	}

	return probe.first(t)

func (f *targetScopeFixture) conversationTurn(t *testing.T) (scopeProbe, int64) {
	t.Helper()
	probe := newScopeProbeProvider()

		t.Fatal(err)
	}

// auditedTools lists the tool names in a guard's audit ring.
func auditedTools(g *guard.Guard) []string {
	var tools []string
	for _, e := range g.Audit() {
		tools = append(tools, e.Tool)
	}
	return tools
}

// The five session entry points — planner round, final planner round, main-agent
// turn, worker intent, conversation turn (chat and retester share it) — each run
// on a context carrying the scope the gate will decide on, with the gate off.
// The planner and the main agent hand their tool calls to Task.TargetGuard, the
// worker to Task.Guard. The target-only guard keeps no record, so the test puts
// a recording guard in its place.
func TestEveryAgentKindCarriesTargetScope(t *testing.T) {
	f := newTargetScopeFixture(t)
	taskSites := []struct {
		name       string
		run        func(*testing.T, *Task) scopeProbe
		wait       time.Duration
		targetOnly bool // the session runs on Task.TargetGuard, not Task.Guard
	}{
		{"planner round", f.plannerLoopRound, intercept.DefaultTargetWaitBound, true},
		{"final planner round", f.finalPlannerRound, 0, true},
		{"main-agent turn", f.mainAgentTurn, intercept.DefaultTargetWaitBound, true},
		{"worker intent", f.workerIntent, intercept.DefaultTargetWaitBound, false},
	}
	for _, site := range taskSites {
		t.Run(site.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			task := f.newTask(t)
			recorder := guard.New()
			task.TargetGuard = recorder
			got := site.run(t, task)
			onTarget, onMain := auditedTools(recorder), auditedTools(task.Guard)
			if site.targetOnly && (len(onTarget) != 1 || onTarget[0] != "LS" || len(onMain) != 0) {
				t.Fatalf("tool calls seen by TargetGuard=%v Guard=%v, want one LS on TargetGuard only", onTarget, onMain)
			}
			if !site.targetOnly && (len(onMain) != 1 || onMain[0] != "LS" || len(onTarget) != 0) {
				t.Fatalf("tool calls seen by TargetGuard=%v Guard=%v, want one LS on Guard only", onTarget, onMain)
			}
			if !got.ok || got.scope.TaskID != task.ID || got.scope.ConversationID != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("scope = %+v (present=%v), want task %s", got.scope, got.ok, task.ID)
			}
			if got.scope.WaitBound != site.wait {
				t.Fatalf("wait bound = %v, want %v", got.scope.WaitBound, site.wait)
			}
			if got.scope.Enabled == nil || got.scope.Enabled() {
				t.Fatal("the gate must be off: the task did not opt in")
			}
			if got.scope.Interceptor != f.m.interceptor {
				t.Fatal("the scope does not carry the interceptor that owns the gate")
			}
		})
	}
	t.Run("conversation turn", func(t *testing.T) {
		got, convID := f.conversationTurn(t)
		if !got.ok || got.scope.ConversationID != convID || got.scope.TaskID != "" {
			t.Fatalf("scope = %+v (present=%v), want conversation %d", got.scope, got.ok, convID)
		}
		if got.scope.WaitBound != intercept.DefaultTargetWaitBound {
			t.Fatalf("wait bound = %v, want %v", got.scope.WaitBound, intercept.DefaultTargetWaitBound)
		}
		if got.scope.Enabled == nil || got.scope.Enabled() {
			t.Fatal("the gate must be off: the conversation did not opt in")
		}
		if got.scope.Interceptor != f.m.interceptor {
			t.Fatal("the scope does not carry the interceptor that owns the gate")
		}
	})
}

// The final settlement round runs on a context a pause cannot cancel and is
// meant to judge, not to explore: a gated call must never wait there. A regular
// round of the same task keeps the default bound.
func TestFinalPlannerRoundHasZeroWait(t *testing.T) {
	f := newTargetScopeFixture(t)
	task := f.newTask(t)
	regular := f.plannerLoopRound(t, task)
	final := f.finalPlannerRound(t, task)
	if !regular.ok || !final.ok {
		t.Fatalf("scope missing: regular=%v final=%v", regular.ok, final.ok)
	}
	if regular.scope.WaitBound <= 0 {
		t.Fatalf("regular round wait bound = %v, want a positive bound", regular.scope.WaitBound)
	}
	if final.scope.WaitBound != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("final round wait bound = %v, want 0", final.scope.WaitBound)
	}
	if final.scope.TaskID != task.ID {
		t.Fatalf("final round scope task = %q, want %s", final.scope.TaskID, task.ID)
	}
}

// With the gate off (the task default) the target-only hooks are a no-op: a call is
// allowed and nothing is written — no intercept row, no audit-ring entry. The
// control runs the same call through the task's full Guard, where a deny rule
// blocks it and logs a row, so the rule and the row count are known to be live.
func TestTargetGateSeamAllowsWithoutDBWrite(t *testing.T) {
	f := newTargetScopeFixture(t)
	task := f.newTask(t)
	ic := f.m.interceptor
	priorTools, err := ic.GetEnabledTools()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = ic.SetEnabledTools(priorTools) })
	if err := ic.SetEnabledTools([]string{"Bash"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	const sentinel = "HIVE_TARGET_SEAM_PROBE"
	rule, err := f.m.pg.CreateInterceptRule("target seam probe", "tool_input", "string", sentinel, "deny", "", 1000000, true, false, 0, "deny")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		_ = f.m.pg.DeleteInterceptRule(rule.ID)
		_, _ = f.m.pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM intercept_pending WHERE task_id=$1`, task.ID)
		ic.Invalidate()
	})
	ic.Invalidate()
	rows := func() int {
		t.Helper()
		var n int
		if err := f.m.pg.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM intercept_pending WHERE task_id=$1`, task.ID).Scan(&n); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return n
	}
	ctx := intercept.WithTaskContext(context.Background(), task.ID, "planner", nil)
	ctx = intercept.WithTargetScope(ctx, task.targetScope(intercept.DefaultTargetWaitBound))
	input := []byte(`{"command":"echo ` + sentinel + `"}`)

	if block, _, _ := task.Guard.Hooks().PreToolUse(ctx, "Bash", input); !block {
		t.Fatal("control: the full guard was expected to deny the call")
	}
	if n := rows(); n != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("control: the full guard logged %d intercept rows, want 1", n)
	}
	ring := len(task.Guard.Audit())

	block, msg, updated := task.TargetGuard.Hooks().PreToolUse(ctx, "Bash", input)
	if block || msg != "" || updated != nil {
		t.Fatalf("target-only hooks: block=%v msg=%q updated=%q, want the call allowed untouched", block, msg, updated)
	}
	task.TargetGuard.Hooks().PostToolUse(ctx, "Bash", input, []byte(`"ok"`), false)
	if n := rows(); n != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("target-only hooks changed the intercept rows: %d, want 1", n)
	}
	if n := len(task.TargetGuard.Audit()); n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("target-only guard wrote %d audit entries, want none", n)
	}
	if n := len(task.Guard.Audit()); n != ring {
		t.Fatalf("the task's audit ring grew from %d to %d entries", ring, n)
	}
}

package server

	"context"

// The gate wired into the server: the exemption API, the exemptions derived
// from the configuration, and the hooks of a task's guards.

// exemptionsOf decodes the "exemptions" (or "derived") list of a response.
func exemptionsOf(t *testing.T, body map[string]any, field string) []db.TargetExemption {
	t.Helper()
	raw, err := json.Marshal(body[field])
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var out []db.TargetExemption
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &out); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s = %s: %v", field, raw, err)
	}
	return out
}

func TestTargetGateExemptionsAPI(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	pg := g.m.pg
	original, _, err := pg.TargetExemptions()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = pg.ReplaceTargetExemptions(original, "test", "restore") })

	// The routes are behind the session, like the rest of the API.
	for _, c := range []struct{ method, path string }{
		{"GET", "/api/target-gate/exemptions"}, {"PUT", "/api/target-gate/exemptions"}, {"GET", "/api/target-gate/exemptions/history"},
	} {
		rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
		g.s.Handler().ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequest(c.method, c.path, strings.NewReader(`{"exemptions":[]}`)))
		if rec.Code != 401 {
			t.Fatalf("%s %s without a token: %d, want 401", c.method, c.path, rec.Code)
		}
	}

	code, body := g.do(t, "GET", "/api/target-gate/exemptions", "")
	if code != 200 || !slices.Equal(exemptionsOf(t, body, "exemptions"), original) || body["digest"] == "" || body["derived"] == nil {
		t.Fatalf("GET: %d %v, want the stored list %+v", code, body, original)
	}

	// PUT replaces the list. Hosts are normalised; host and port are exact.
	code, body = g.do(t, "PUT", "/api/target-gate/exemptions",
		`{"exemptions":[{"host":"Mirror.Example.ORG.","port":443,"note":"internal mirror"},{"host":"10.0.0.5","port":8080},{"host":"FD12:3456::5","port":8080}]}`)
	want := []db.TargetExemption{{Host: "mirror.example.org", Port: 443, Note: "internal mirror"}, {Host: "10.0.0.5", Port: 8080}, {Host: "fd12:3456::5", Port: 8080}}
	if code != 200 || !slices.Equal(exemptionsOf(t, body, "exemptions"), want) {
		t.Fatalf("PUT: %d %v, want %+v", code, body, want)
	}
	digest, _ := body["digest"].(string)
	code, body = g.do(t, "GET", "/api/target-gate/exemptions", "")
	if code != 200 || !slices.Equal(exemptionsOf(t, body, "exemptions"), want) || body["digest"] != digest || digest == "" {
		t.Fatalf("GET after PUT: %d %v", code, body)
	}

	// Refused entries: 400, and the stored list does not change.
	for name, entry := range map[string]string{
		"metadata address":         `{"host":"169.254.169.254","port":80}`,
		"metadata address, v6":     `{"host":"fd00:ec2::254","port":80}`,
		"metadata address, cloud":  `{"host":"100.100.100.200","port":80}`,
		"link-local v6":            `{"host":"fe80::1","port":80}`,
		"loopback":                 `{"host":"127.0.0.1","port":8080}`,
		"loopback as a number":     `{"host":"2130706433","port":8080}`,
		"loopback v6":              `{"host":"::1","port":8080}`,
		"unspecified":              `{"host":"0.0.0.0","port":80}`,
		"multicast":                `{"host":"224.0.0.1","port":80}`,
		"wildcard":                 `{"host":"*.example.org","port":443}`,
		"suffix":                   `{"host":".example.org","port":443}`,
		"range":                    `{"host":"10.0.0.0/8","port":443}`,
		"url":                      `{"host":"https://mirror.example.org/","port":443}`,
		"host with a port":         `{"host":"mirror.example.org:443","port":443}`,
		"no port":                  `{"host":"mirror.example.org"}`,
		"port out of range":        `{"host":"mirror.example.org","port":70000}`,
		"no host":                  `{"port":443}`,
		"one bad entry among good": `{"host":"pypi.org","port":443},{"host":"169.254.169.254","port":80}`,
	} {
		code, body := g.do(t, "PUT", "/api/target-gate/exemptions", `{"exemptions":[`+entry+`]}`)
		if code != 400 || body["error"] == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: %d %v, want 400", name, code, body)
		}
	}
	if code, _ := g.do(t, "PUT", "/api/target-gate/exemptions", `not json`); code != 400 {
		t.Fatalf("malformed body: %d, want 400", code)
	}
	if list, _, err := pg.TargetExemptions(); err != nil || !slices.Equal(list, want) {
		t.Fatalf("stored list after the refused changes = %+v, %v; want it unchanged", list, err)
	}

	// The history holds the one change that was made, with who made it.
	code, body = g.do(t, "GET", "/api/target-gate/exemptions/history", "")
	changes, _ := body["changes"].([]any)
	if code != 200 || len(changes) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("history: %d %v", code, body)
	}
	last, _ := changes[0].(map[string]any)
	if last["changed_by"] != "HIVE" || last["digest"] != digest || len(exemptionsOf(t, last, "after")) != 3 || !slices.Equal(exemptionsOf(t, last, "before"), original) {
		t.Fatalf("last change = %v", last)
	}

	// An empty list is a valid list.
	if code, body := g.do(t, "PUT", "/api/target-gate/exemptions", `{}`); code != 200 || len(exemptionsOf(t, body, "exemptions")) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("empty list: %d %v", code, body)
	}
	if code, body := g.do(t, "GET", "/api/target-gate/exemptions", ""); code != 200 || body["exemptions"] == nil || len(exemptionsOf(t, body, "exemptions")) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("GET of the empty list: %d %v", code, body)
	}
}

// The exemptions of the platform's own endpoints are derived from the
// configuration on every call: LLM gateways, profile proxies, the search
// backend in use, the search proxy and the global egress proxy.
func TestTargetGateEndpointsFollowConfig(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	derived := func() []string {
		var out []string
		for _, e := range g.m.interceptor.DerivedExemptions() {
			out = append(out, db.TargetKey(e.Host, e.Port))
		}
		return out
	}
	has := func(key string) bool { return slices.Contains(derived(), key) }

	name := fmt.Sprintf("target-gate-endpoints-%d", time.Now().UnixNano())
	id, err := g.m.pg.SaveProfile(&db.LLMProfile{Name: name, Format: "openai", BaseURL: "https://LLM-gateway.example.net:8443/v1",
		Proxy: "http://user:secret@llm-proxy.example.net:3128", Model: "m", APIKey: "k"})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = g.m.pg.DeleteProfile(id) })
	for _, key := range []string{"llm-gateway.example.net:8443", "llm-proxy.example.net:3128"} {
		if !has(key) {
			t.Fatalf("derived = %v, want the profile endpoint %s", derived(), key)
		}
	}
	for _, e := range derived() {
		if strings.Contains(e, "secret") || strings.Contains(e, "user") {
			t.Fatalf("a derived exemption carries credentials: %s", e)
		}
	}

	on, backend, _, _, proxy := g.m.WebSearch()
	globalProxy := g.m.GlobalProxy()
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		_ = g.m.SetWebSearch(on, backend, nil, nil, &proxy)
		_ = g.m.SetGlobalProxy(globalProxy)
	})
	searchProxy := "http://search-proxy.example.net:8118"
	if err := g.m.SetWebSearch(true, "tavily", nil, nil, &searchProxy); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := g.m.SetGlobalProxy("socks5://egress.example.net:1080"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, key := range []string{"api.tavily.com:443", "search-proxy.example.net:8118", "egress.example.net:1080"} {
		if !has(key) {
			t.Fatalf("derived = %v, want %s", derived(), key)
		}
	}
	// The configuration changes: so do the exemptions.
	none := ""
	if err := g.m.SetWebSearch(true, "ddgs", nil, nil, &none); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := g.m.SetGlobalProxy(""); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := g.m.pg.DeleteProfile(id); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !has("html.duckduckgo.com:443") {
		t.Fatalf("derived = %v, want the keyless search backend", derived())
	}
	for _, key := range []string{"api.tavily.com:443", "search-proxy.example.net:8118", "egress.example.net:1080", "llm-gateway.example.net:8443", "llm-proxy.example.net:3128"} {
		if has(key) {
			t.Fatalf("derived = %v, still holds %s after the configuration changed", derived(), key)
		}
	}
	// Search off: its backend is not exempt.
	if err := g.m.SetWebSearch(false, "ddgs", nil, nil, nil); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if has("html.duckduckgo.com:443") {
		t.Fatalf("derived = %v, want no search backend while search is off", derived())
	}
	// The API shows them, read-only.
	if code, body := g.do(t, "GET", "/api/target-gate/exemptions", ""); code != 200 || body["derived"] == nil {
		t.Fatalf("GET: %d %v", code, body)
	}
}

// An approval of a request that displays no address is refused with 422. The

func TestInterceptDecideRefusesEmptyPinOverHTTP(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)

	}
}

// The hooks of a task run the gate with the task's own scope: the worker
// guard and the target-only guard of the planner and the main agent. The flag
// is the task's, read on every call.
func TestTaskGuardsRunTargetGate(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	task := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{})
	scope := taskRef(t, task)
	pg := g.m.pg
	const fetch = `{"url":"http://203.0.113.7:8080/admin"}`
	ctxOf := func(agentName string, wait time.Duration) context.Context {
		return intercept.WithTargetScope(intercept.WithTaskContext(context.Background(), task.ID, agentName, nil), task.targetScope(wait))
	}
	targetRows := func() int {
		t.Helper()
		var n int
		if err := pg.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM intercept_pending WHERE task_id=$1 AND decision_source='target'`, task.ID).Scan(&n); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return n
	}
	hook := func(hooks interface {
		PreToolUse(context.Context, string, []byte) (bool, string, []byte)
	}, ctx context.Context) (bool, string) {
		block, msg, _ := hooks.PreToolUse(ctx, "WebFetch", []byte(fetch))
		return block, msg
	}

	// Gate off, the default: both guards pass the call and write nothing.
	for name, hooks := range map[string]interface {
		PreToolUse(context.Context, string, []byte) (bool, string, []byte)
	}{"worker": task.Guard.Hooks(), "planner": task.TargetGuard.Hooks()} {
		if block, msg := hook(hooks, ctxOf(name, 0)); block {
			t.Fatalf("gate off, %s: blocked: %s", name, msg)
		}
	}
	if n := targetRows(); n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("gate off: %d target rows, want none", n)
	}

	// Gate on through the API: the next call of each guard is stopped. With
	// wait bound 0 it does not wait, and the one request stays open.
	if code, _ := g.do(t, "PATCH", "/api/tasks/"+task.ID, `{"target_gate":true}`); code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("switch the gate on: %d", code)
	}
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name  string
		hooks interface {
			PreToolUse(context.Context, string, []byte) (bool, string, []byte)
		}
	}{{"planner", task.TargetGuard.Hooks()}, {"worker", task.Guard.Hooks()}} {
		block, msg := hook(c.hooks, ctxOf(c.name, 0))
		if !block || !strings.Contains(msg, "TARGET_APPROVAL_PENDING: target 203.0.113.7:8080: ") {
			t.Fatalf("gate on, %s: block=%v msg=%q", c.name, block, msg)
		}
	}
	var id int64
	var agentName string
	var open int
	if err := pg.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*), min(id), min(agent_name) FROM intercept_pending
WHERE task_id=$1 AND status='pending' AND target_key='203.0.113.7:8080'`, task.ID).Scan(&open, &id, &agentName); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if open != 1 || agentName != "planner" {
		t.Fatalf("%d open requests by %q, want one, opened by the planner's call", open, agentName)
	}
	// The planner's block is in the ring of its own guard, not in the task's.
	if audit := task.TargetGuard.Audit(); len(audit) != 1 || audit[0].Action != "block" {
		t.Fatalf("target-only ring = %+v, want the one block", audit)
	}
	for _, e := range task.Guard.Audit() {
		if e.Action == "block" && !strings.Contains(e.Reason, "TARGET_APPROVAL_PENDING") {
			t.Fatalf("unexpected entry in the task ring: %+v", e)
		}
	}

	// One click through the API pins the address for the task; both guards pass.
	if code, _ := g.do(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/api/intercept/pending/%d/decide", id), `{"decision":"allowed"}`); code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("decide: %d", code)
	}
	if pins, err := pg.ListTargetPins(scope); err != nil || len(pins) != 1 || pins[0].Host != "203.0.113.7" || pins[0].Port != 8080 ||
		!slices.Equal(pins[0].PinnedIPs, []string{"203.0.113.7"}) || pins[0].DecidedBy != "HIVE" {
		t.Fatalf("pins = %+v, %v", pins, err)
	}
	ring := len(task.TargetGuard.Audit())
	for name, hooks := range map[string]interface {
		PreToolUse(context.Context, string, []byte) (bool, string, []byte)
	}{"worker": task.Guard.Hooks(), "planner": task.TargetGuard.Hooks()} {
		if block, msg := hook(hooks, ctxOf(name, 0)); block {
			t.Fatalf("pinned, %s: blocked: %s", name, msg)
		}
	}
	if n := len(task.TargetGuard.Audit()); n != ring {
		t.Fatalf("a passing planner call added %d entries to the ring", n-ring)
	}
	// Gate off again: the gate is out of the way at once.
	if code, _ := g.do(t, "PATCH", "/api/tasks/"+task.ID, `{"target_gate":false}`); code != 200 {
		t.Fatal("switch the gate off")
	}
	rows := targetRows()
	if block, _, _ := task.Guard.Hooks().PreToolUse(ctxOf("worker", 0), "WebFetch", []byte(`{"url":"http://198.51.100.200/"}`)); block || targetRows() != rows {
		t.Fatalf("gate off again: block=%v, %d new target rows", block, targetRows()-rows)
	}
}

// The platform's own tools read and write the platform's records: the gate
// must find no target in their input, or every finding and every intent that
// mentions a URL would ask for an approval. A tool added to these sets has to
// be added to the gate's list of tools without a target.
func TestHostToolsDeclareNoTarget(t *testing.T) {
	s := &Server{}
	var tools []actool.CoreTool
	tools = append(tools, s.orchestrationTools()...)
	tools = append(tools, s.findingRetestTools()...)
	tools = append(tools, s.platformTools()...)
	tools = append(tools, traffic.SeedToolMetas()...)
	if len(tools) < 25 {
		t.Fatalf("only %d host tools found", len(tools))
	}
	// The tools that set up a custom tool or an MCP server take an endpoint of
	// the model's choosing. They are scanned like any unknown tool: that
	// endpoint is a target.
	scanned := map[string]bool{"create_custom_tool": true, "update_custom_tool": true, "create_mcp": true, "update_mcp": true, "mcp_status": true}
	input := []byte(`{"task_id":1,"description":"test https://app.example.com/ and 203.0.113.7:8443","command":"curl https://app.example.com/","q":"host:app.example.com:443"}`)
	for _, tool := range tools {
		targets := intercept.ExtractTargets(tool.Name(), input)
		if scanned[tool.Name()] {
			if len(targets) == 0 {
				t.Errorf("%s: no target read", tool.Name())
			}
			delete(scanned, tool.Name())
		} else if len(targets) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("%s: the gate reads targets %+v from a platform tool", tool.Name(), targets)
		}
	}
	if len(scanned) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("tools that no longer exist: %v", scanned)
	}
}

package server

import (
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"sync/atomic"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

// Step 1.9: the redirect hops of the custom http tool and of a worker's
// WebFetch go through the target gate.

// redirectingServer answers every request with a redirect to location and
// counts the requests. Its host:port is an IP literal: the gate never resolves it.
func redirectingServer(t *testing.T, location string) (srv *httptest.Server, hits *atomic.Int64, key string) {
	t.Helper()
	hits = &atomic.Int64{}
	srv = httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		hits.Add(1)
		http.Redirect(w, r, location, http.StatusFound)
	}))
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)
	return srv, hits, srv.Listener.Addr().String()
}

func decide(t *testing.T, g *gateServer, id int64, decision string) {
	t.Helper()
	if code, body := g.do(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/api/intercept/pending/%d/decide", id), `{"decision":"`+decision+`"}`); code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("decide %d: %d %v", id, code, body)
	}
}

// A custom http tool whose rendered URL is pinned, and which redirects to a
// target no pin covers: the hop is not followed, one request is opened for its
// target, and the call fails at once. After the approval the same call follows.
func TestCustomHTTPRedirectTargetGated(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	on := true
	task := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{TargetGate: &on})
	pg := g.m.pg
	final, finalHits, fhost, fport := countingServer(t)
	finalKey := net.JoinHostPort(fhost, fport)
	start, startHits, startKey := redirectingServer(t, final.URL+"/final")

	tool := g.s.buildCustomTool(&db.Tool{Key: "probe_redirect", Kind: "http",
		Exec: execJSON(t, map[string]any{"method": "GET", "url": start.URL + "/start"})})
	// The rendered URL itself first: its request, approved.
	if out, isErr := callTool(t, tool, gatedCtx(task, 0), `{}`, nil); !isErr || !strings.Contains(out, "TARGET_APPROVAL_PENDING") || startHits.Load() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("rendered URL: error=%v out=%q", isErr, out)
	}
	id, _, _, ok := openTargetRequest(t, pg, task.ID, startKey)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("no request for the rendered URL")
	}
	decide(t, g, id, "allowed")

	// The wait bound is long: the hop must not use it.
	began := time.Now()
	out, isErr := callTool(t, tool, gatedCtx(task, time.Minute), `{}`, nil)
	if !isErr || !strings.Contains(out, "TARGET_APPROVAL_PENDING") || !strings.Contains(out, start.URL+"/start redirects to "+finalKey) {
		t.Fatalf("redirect to an unpinned target: error=%v out=%q", isErr, out)
	}
	if elapsed := time.Since(began); elapsed > 10*time.Second {
		t.Fatalf("the hop waited %v", elapsed)
	}
	if startHits.Load() != 1 || finalHits.Load() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("hits origin=%d target=%d, want the target untouched", startHits.Load(), finalHits.Load())
	}
	hopID, toolName, toolInput, ok := openTargetRequest(t, pg, task.ID, finalKey)
	if !ok || toolName != "probe_redirect" || !strings.Contains(toolInput, final.URL+"/final") || !strings.Contains(toolInput, start.URL+"/start") {
		t.Fatalf("request for the hop: ok=%v tool=%q input=%s", ok, toolName, toolInput)
	}
	var requests int
	if err := pg.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM intercept_pending WHERE task_id=$1 AND target_key IS NOT NULL`, task.ID).Scan(&requests); err != nil || requests != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("%d requests, %v; want the origin's and the hop's", requests, err)
	}

	decide(t, g, hopID, "allowed")
	if out, isErr := callTool(t, tool, gatedCtx(task, 0), `{}`, nil); isErr || !strings.Contains(out, "probe-reached") || finalHits.Load() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("after the approval: error=%v out=%q target hits=%d", isErr, out, finalHits.Load())
	}
}

// The custom-tool test endpoint has no approval scope (D14): its redirects are
// followed as before, and nothing is written.
func TestCustomToolTestEndpointRedirectUngated(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	on := true
	g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{TargetGate: &on})
	final, finalHits, _, _ := countingServer(t)
	start, _, _ := redirectingServer(t, final.URL+"/final")
	count := func() int {
		var n int
		if err := g.m.pg.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM intercept_pending WHERE decision_source='target' OR target_key IS NOT NULL`).Scan(&n); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return n
	}
	before := count()
	code, out := g.do(t, "POST", "/api/tools/custom/test", fmt.Sprintf(`{"kind":"http","exec":{"url":%q}}`, start.URL+"/start"))
	if code != 200 || out["is_error"] != false || !strings.Contains(fmt.Sprint(out["output"]), "probe-reached") || finalHits.Load() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("test endpoint: %d %v target hits=%d", code, out, finalHits.Load())
	}
	if after := count(); after != before {
		t.Fatalf("the test endpoint wrote %d target rows", after-before)
	}
}

// A gated worker's WebFetch end to end: the origin is approved at the hook, the
// redirect stops at the hop with TARGET_APPROVAL_PENDING and leaves one request
// open; once it is approved through the API, the same call follows.
func TestRedirectRequestSurvivesAndRetryPasses(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	on := true
	task := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{TargetGate: &on})
	pg := g.m.pg
	final, finalHits, fhost, fport := countingServer(t)
	finalKey := net.JoinHostPort(fhost, fport)
	start, startHits, startKey := redirectingServer(t, final.URL+"/final")
	p := &toolScript{calls: fetches(start.URL+"/start", start.URL+"/start"), results: make(chan string, 16),
		hold: map[int64]chan struct{}{2: make(chan struct{})}}
	done := runScriptedWorker(t, g, task, p)

	var id int64
	waitUntil(t, "the request for the origin", func() bool {
		var ok bool
		id, _, _, ok = openTargetRequest(t, pg, task.ID, startKey)
		return ok
	})
	decide(t, g, id, "allowed")
	if r := p.next(t); !strings.Contains(r, "TARGET_APPROVAL_PENDING") || !strings.Contains(r, "redirects to "+finalKey) {
		t.Fatalf("first call: %q", r)
	}
	if startHits.Load() != 1 || finalHits.Load() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("hits origin=%d target=%d, want the target untouched", startHits.Load(), finalHits.Load())
	}
	hopID, toolName, _, ok := openTargetRequest(t, pg, task.ID, finalKey)
	if !ok || toolName != "WebFetch" {
		t.Fatalf("request for the hop: ok=%v tool=%q", ok, toolName)
	}
	detail, err := pg.GetInterceptDetail(hopID)
	if err != nil || detail == nil || detail.Audit == nil || len(detail.Audit.Targets) != 1 || detail.Audit.Targets[0].RedirectFrom != startKey {
		t.Fatalf("hop request detail = %+v, %v", detail, err)
	}

	decide(t, g, hopID, "allowed")
	close(p.hold[2])
	if r := p.next(t); !strings.Contains(r, "probe-reached") || finalHits.Load() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("the same call after the approval: %q target hits=%d", r, finalHits.Load())
	}
	select {
	case <-done:
	case <-time.After(60 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the worker run did not end")
	}
}

package server

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"

	"fmt"

	"strconv"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

func newAdmissionTestServer(m *Manager, available func(*Task) bool) *Server {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	cancel()
	e := NewEngine(m)
	planner, worker := new(agent.Planner), new(agent.Worker)
	e.SetAuthoritativeAgentResolver(func(task *Task) (*agent.Planner, *agent.Worker) {
		if available == nil || available(task) {
			return planner, worker
		}
		return nil, nil
	})
	return &Server{m: m, engine: e, ctx: ctx, chatBusy: map[string]bool{}, chatCancel: map[string]context.CancelCauseFunc{}}
}

func restoreConcurrencySetting(t *testing.T, m *Manager) func() {
	t.Helper()
	enabled, limit := m.ConcurrencyLimit()
	if limit < 1 {
		limit = defaultConcurrencyLimit
	}
	return func() {
		if err := m.SetConcurrency(enabled, limit); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("restore concurrency setting: %v", err)
		}
	}
}

func TestAdmitAlreadyRunningTaskDoesNotQueueAfterLimitDecrease(t *testing.T) {
	m, err := NewManager(t.TempDir(), "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) - skipping", err)
	}
	defer m.Close()

	oldEnabled, oldLimit := m.ConcurrencyLimit()
	if oldLimit < 1 {
		oldLimit = defaultConcurrencyLimit
	}
	defer m.SetConcurrency(oldEnabled, oldLimit)
	if err := m.SetConcurrency(true, 1); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	running, err := m.CreateTask("already admitted", "accept follow-up", nil, 0, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	holder, err := m.CreateTask("other admitted task", "occupy lowered limit", nil, 0, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer func() {
		_, _ = m.DeleteTask(running.ID, DeleteTaskOptions{})
		_, _ = m.DeleteTask(holder.ID, DeleteTaskOptions{})
	}()

	s := newAdmissionTestServer(m, nil)
	// Simulate a task whose long-lived loops were admitted before the limit was
	// lowered. The other live task makes the current count exceed the new limit.
	s.engine.started.Store(running.ID, true)
	queued, err := s.admitTask(running, "resume")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if queued || running.Queued {
		t.Fatalf("already-running task was re-queued: queued=%v task=%+v", queued, running)
	}
}

func TestAdmissionDoesNotOverwriteConcurrentTerminalStatus(t *testing.T) {
	m, err := NewManager(t.TempDir(), "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) - skipping", err)
	}
	defer m.Close()
	defer restoreConcurrencySetting(t, m)()
	if err := m.SetConcurrency(false, defaultConcurrencyLimit); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	task, err := m.CreateTask("stale admission", "preserve terminal writer", nil, 0, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer func() { _, _ = m.DeleteTask(task.ID, DeleteTaskOptions{}) }()

	// Model an Engine terminal commit after admission captured its in-memory
	// snapshot but before the scheduler UPDATE. Direct DB use intentionally leaves
	// the live handle stale at its old status for this deterministic interleaving.
	taskID, _ := strconv.ParseInt(task.ID, 10, 64)
	if err := m.pg.SetStatus(taskID, "done"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s := newAdmissionTestServer(m, nil)
	if _, err := s.admitTask(task, "resume"); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("stale admission overwrote a concurrent terminal transition")
	}
	stored, err := m.pg.GetTask(taskID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if stored == nil || stored.Status != "done" || stored.Queued || stored.Paused {
		t.Fatalf("terminal state changed by stale admission: %+v", stored)
	}
}

func TestAdmitKeepsQueuedBootstrapMode(t *testing.T) {

func TestTimedOutTaskRevivalResetsClockAndSettlingAcrossFIFO(t *testing.T) {
	m, err := NewManager(t.TempDir(), "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) - skipping", err)
	}
	defer m.Close()
	defer restoreConcurrencySetting(t, m)()
	if err := m.SetConcurrency(true, 1); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	holder, err := m.CreateTask("timeout revival holder", "occupy slot", nil, 0, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	task, err := m.CreateTask("timed out follow-up", "run with a fresh clock", nil, 120, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer func() {
		_, _ = m.DeleteTask(holder.ID, DeleteTaskOptions{})
		_, _ = m.DeleteTask(task.ID, DeleteTaskOptions{})
	}()
	if _, err := m.StampTaskFirstRun(task.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	oldClock := task.lifecycleSnapshot()
	if oldClock.FirstRunAt == 0 || oldClock.DeadlineAt == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("test setup did not stamp the original clock: %+v", oldClock)
	}
	if err := m.SetTaskStatus(task.ID, "timeout"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	s := newAdmissionTestServer(m, nil)
	s.engine.settling.Store(task.ID, true)
	s.engine.deadline.Store(task.ID, oldClock.DeadlineAt)
	s.engine.stamped.Store(task.ID, true)
	s.engine.coordStarted.Store(task.ID, true)

	queued, err := s.admitTask(task, "resume")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	queuedState := task.lifecycleSnapshot()
	if !queued || !queuedState.Queued || queuedState.Status != "running" ||
		queuedState.FirstRunAt != 0 || queuedState.DeadlineAt != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("timed-out task was not reset before FIFO wait: queued=%v state=%+v", queued, queuedState)
	}
	if s.engine.isSettling(task.ID) {
		t.Fatal("timed-out task retained the old settling gate while queued")
	}
	if _, ok := s.engine.deadline.Load(task.ID); ok {
		t.Fatal("timed-out task retained the old in-memory deadline")
	}
	if _, ok := s.engine.stamped.Load(task.ID); ok {
		t.Fatal("timed-out task retained the old first-run stamp")
	}
	stored, err := m.pg.GetTask(mustTaskID(t, task.ID))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if stored == nil || stored.TimeoutSeconds != 120 || stored.FirstRunAt != nil || stored.DeadlineAt != nil {
		t.Fatalf("persisted timeout revival clock/config mismatch: %+v", stored)
	}

	// Release the only slot and promote the revived task. The test server uses a
	// cancelled root context so no real Agent call races these state assertions.
	s.engine.Pause(holder.ID, agent.AbortPausedByUser)
	if err := m.ApplyTaskPause(holder.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s.reconcileConcurrency()
	runningState := task.lifecycleSnapshot()
	if runningState.Queued || runningState.Paused || s.engine.IsPaused(task.ID) || s.engine.isSettling(task.ID) {
		t.Fatalf("revived task did not leave FIFO ready to execute: state=%+v enginePaused=%v settling=%v",
			runningState, s.engine.IsPaused(task.ID), s.engine.isSettling(task.ID))
	}
	if execCtx := s.engine.execContextFor(context.Background(), task.ID); execCtx.Err() != nil {
		t.Fatalf("revived task did not receive a live execution context: %v", context.Cause(execCtx))
	}
	if _, ok := s.engine.coordStarted.Load(task.ID); !ok {
		t.Fatal("revived timeout task did not start a fresh deadline coordinator")
	}
}

func TestQueuedTaskCanPauseAndResumeAtFIFOTail(t *testing.T) {
	m, err := NewManager(t.TempDir(), "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) - skipping", err)
	}
	defer m.Close()
	defer restoreConcurrencySetting(t, m)()
	if err := m.SetConcurrency(true, 1); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	holder, err := m.CreateTask("slot holder", "hold", nil, 0, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	task, err := m.CreateTask("pause queued", "resume later", nil, 0, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer func() {
		_, _ = m.DeleteTask(holder.ID, DeleteTaskOptions{})
		_, _ = m.DeleteTask(task.ID, DeleteTaskOptions{})
	}()
	s := newAdmissionTestServer(m, nil)
	if err := m.SetTaskPaused(task.ID, true); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s.engine.Pause(task.ID, agent.AbortPausedByUser)

	first, err := s.applyTaskControl(task, "resume")
	if err != nil || !first.Queued || task.QueuedAt == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("first resume: result=%+v task=%+v err=%v", first, task, err)
	}
	firstQueuedAt := task.QueuedAt
	if _, err := s.applyTaskControl(task, "pause"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !task.Paused || task.Queued || task.QueuedAt != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("pause did not leave queue: %+v", task)
	}
	time.Sleep(2 * time.Millisecond)
	second, err := s.applyTaskControl(task, "resume")
	if err != nil || !second.Queued {
		t.Fatalf("second resume: result=%+v task=%+v err=%v", second, task, err)
	}
	if task.QueuedAt <= firstQueuedAt {
		t.Fatalf("resumed task did not move to FIFO tail: first=%d second=%d", firstQueuedAt, task.QueuedAt)
	}
}

func TestReadyFIFOIsAdmittedBeforeNewTask(t *testing.T) {
	m, err := NewManager(t.TempDir(), "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) - skipping", err)
	}
	defer m.Close()
	defer restoreConcurrencySetting(t, m)()
	if err := m.SetConcurrency(true, 2); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	holder, err := m.CreateTask("slot holder", "hold", nil, 0, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	older, err := m.CreateTask("older queued", "first", nil, 0, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	incoming, err := m.CreateTask("new admission", "second", nil, 0, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer func() {
		_, _ = m.DeleteTask(holder.ID, DeleteTaskOptions{})
		_, _ = m.DeleteTask(older.ID, DeleteTaskOptions{})
		_, _ = m.DeleteTask(incoming.ID, DeleteTaskOptions{})
	}()
	s := newAdmissionTestServer(m, nil)
	if err := m.EnqueueTask(older.ID, "resume"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s.engine.Pause(older.ID, agent.AbortPausedByOrchestrator)

	queued, err := s.admitTask(incoming, "resume")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !queued || !incoming.Queued || incoming.QueuedAt <= older.QueuedAt {
		t.Fatalf("new task bypassed ready FIFO: queued=%v older=%+v incoming=%+v", queued, older, incoming)
	}
	s.reconcileConcurrency()
	if older.Queued || !incoming.Queued {
		t.Fatalf("FIFO promotion order wrong: older=%+v incoming=%+v", older, incoming)
	}
}

func TestUnavailableTaskReleasesSlotForReadyQueue(t *testing.T) {
