	}
}

func TestTaskLLMStreamDoesNotSwitchForOrdinaryErrors(t *testing.T) {
	// Not parallel: overrides the package-level backoff so the retryable cases
	// don't sleep. Serial tests never overlap the parallel batch, so this is safe.
	defer withZeroRetryBackoff()()
	tests := []string{
		"openai: status 429: rate limit exceeded",
		"openai: status 401: invalid api key",
		"openai: status 500: internal server error",
		"dial tcp: network is unreachable",
	}
	for _, message := range tests {
		t.Run(message, func(t *testing.T) {
			resetLLMFailStreaksForTest() // package-global streaks must not leak across subtests
			provider := &scriptedLLMProvider{err: errors.New(message)}
			exhausted := 0
			hooks := taskLLMStreamHooks{
				current: func(ctx context.Context) (taskLLMSelection, error) {
					return taskLLMSelection{profileID: 11, provider: provider}, nil
				},
				exhaust: func(taskLLMSelection, error) (db.TaskLLMTransition, error) {
					exhausted++
					return db.TaskLLMTransition{}, nil
				},
			}
			_, err := collectTaskLLMStream(streamTaskLLM(context.Background(), "7", llm.CompletionRequest{}, hooks))
			if err == nil || err.Error() != message {
				t.Fatalf("error=%v, want %q", err, message)
			}
			if exhausted != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("ordinary error changed failover state %d times", exhausted)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestTaskLLMStreamAdvancesAfterMidStreamQuotaWithoutReplay(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	quota := errors.New("anthropic: status 402: credit balance is too low")
	first := &scriptedLLMProvider{
		events: []llm.StreamEvent{{Type: llm.SETextDelta, Text: "partial"}},
		err:    quota,
	}
	second := &scriptedLLMProvider{events: []llm.StreamEvent{{Type: llm.SETextDelta, Text: "next-call"}}}
	active := int64(11)
	hooks := taskLLMStreamHooks{
		current: func(ctx context.Context) (taskLLMSelection, error) {
			if active == 11 {
				return taskLLMSelection{profileID: 11, provider: first}, nil
			}
			return taskLLMSelection{profileID: 22, provider: second}, nil
		},
		exhaust: func(taskLLMSelection, error) (db.TaskLLMTransition, error) {
			active = 22
			next := active
			return db.TaskLLMTransition{PreviousProfileID: 11, NextProfileID: &next, Advanced: true}, nil
		},
	}

	events, err := collectTaskLLMStream(streamTaskLLM(context.Background(), "7", llm.CompletionRequest{}, hooks))
	if len(events) != 1 || events[0].Text != "partial" || err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("mid-stream result events=%+v err=%v", events, err)
	}
	if first.calls != 1 || second.calls != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("mid-stream call was replayed: first=%d second=%d", first.calls, second.calls)
	}

	nextEvents, nextErr := collectTaskLLMStream(streamTaskLLM(context.Background(), "7", llm.CompletionRequest{}, hooks))
	if nextErr != nil || len(nextEvents) != 1 || nextEvents[0].Text != "next-call" || second.calls != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("next call did not use fallback: events=%+v err=%v calls=%d", nextEvents, nextErr, second.calls)
	}
}

func TestTaskLLMStreamMarkFailureAfterToolStartSkipsWorkerReplay(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	quota := errors.New("openai: status 402: insufficient_quota")
	markFailure := errors.New("database temporarily unavailable")
	provider := &scriptedLLMProvider{
		events: []llm.StreamEvent{{Type: llm.SEToolUseStart}},
		err:    quota,
	}
	hooks := taskLLMStreamHooks{
		current: func(ctx context.Context) (taskLLMSelection, error) {
			return taskLLMSelection{profileID: 11, provider: provider}, nil
		},
		exhaust: func(taskLLMSelection, error) (db.TaskLLMTransition, error) {
			return db.TaskLLMTransition{}, markFailure
		},
	}

	events, err := collectTaskLLMStream(streamTaskLLM(context.Background(), "7", llm.CompletionRequest{}, hooks))
	if len(events) != 1 || events[0].Type != llm.SEToolUseStart || err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("committed tool stream events=%+v err=%v", events, err)
	}
	if !isTaskLLMRuntimeError(err) {
		t.Fatalf("committed mark failure must be router-classified: %T %v", err, err)
	}
	if retryableWorkerModelError(harness.ReasonModelError, err) {
		t.Fatal("worker must not replay after a committed tool stream when quota persistence fails")
	}
	if provider.calls != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("provider calls=%d, want 1", provider.calls)
	}
}

func TestTaskLLMRuntimeErrorSkipsWorkerReplay(t *testing.T) {
	partialStreamErr := &taskLLMError{
		taskID:         "7",
		chainExhausted: false,
		cause:          errors.New("insufficient_quota after partial output"),
	}
	if retryableWorkerModelError(harness.ReasonModelError, partialStreamErr) {
		t.Fatal("worker must not replay an intent after the task router handled a mid-stream quota error")
	}
	if !retryableWorkerModelError(harness.ReasonModelError, errors.New("temporary network error")) {
		t.Fatal("ordinary model errors should retain the existing worker retry behavior")
	}
}

// A transient pre-commit stream failure (200-then-drop / overloaded / 5xx) is
// retried on the SAME provider, without switching profiles, and succeeds once the
// blip clears — instead of surfacing as a model_error.
func TestTaskLLMStreamRetriesTransientPreCommitOnSameProvider(t *testing.T) {
	defer withZeroRetryBackoff()()
	provider := &flakyThenOKProvider{
		failCount: 2, // fail twice, succeed on the 3rd attempt (initial + 2 retries)
		failErr:   errors.New("anthropic: overloaded_error"),
		okEvents:  []llm.StreamEvent{{Type: llm.SEMessageStart}, {Type: llm.SETextDelta, Text: "ok"}},
	}
	exhausted := 0
	hooks := taskLLMStreamHooks{
		current: func(ctx context.Context) (taskLLMSelection, error) {
			return taskLLMSelection{profileID: 11, provider: provider}, nil
		},
		exhaust: func(taskLLMSelection, error) (db.TaskLLMTransition, error) {
			exhausted++
			return db.TaskLLMTransition{}, nil
		},
	}
	events, err := collectTaskLLMStream(streamTaskLLM(context.Background(), "7", llm.CompletionRequest{}, hooks))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("transient pre-commit failure should have been retried to success, got %v", err)
	}
	if provider.calls != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("provider calls=%d, want 3 (1 initial + 2 retries)", provider.calls)
	}
	if exhausted != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("same-provider retry must not change failover state (exhausted=%d)", exhausted)
	}
	if len(events) == 0 || events[len(events)-1].Text != "ok" {
		t.Fatalf("recovered stream missing its committed output: %+v", events)
	}
}

// Once retries are exhausted, the transient error is surfaced (becoming a
// model_error upstream) after exactly sameProviderStreamRetries+1 attempts.
func TestTaskLLMStreamSurfacesTransientAfterRetriesExhausted(t *testing.T) {
	defer withZeroRetryBackoff()()
	provider := &flakyThenOKProvider{
		failCount: 99, // never recovers
		failErr:   errors.New("dial tcp: connection reset by peer"),
	}
	hooks := taskLLMStreamHooks{
		current: func(ctx context.Context) (taskLLMSelection, error) {
			return taskLLMSelection{profileID: 11, provider: provider}, nil
		},
		exhaust: func(taskLLMSelection, error) (db.TaskLLMTransition, error) {
			return db.TaskLLMTransition{}, nil
		},
	}
	_, err := collectTaskLLMStream(streamTaskLLM(context.Background(), "7", llm.CompletionRequest{}, hooks))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("persistent transient failure must still surface an error")
	}
	if provider.calls != sameProviderStreamRetries+1 {
		t.Fatalf("provider calls=%d, want %d", provider.calls, sameProviderStreamRetries+1)
	}
}

// A deterministic 4xx rejection is NOT retried on the same provider — replaying
// the identical request everywhere fails the same way.
func TestTaskLLMStreamDoesNotRetryDeterministicRejection(t *testing.T) {
	defer withZeroRetryBackoff()()
	provider := &flakyThenOKProvider{
		failCount: 99,
		failErr:   errors.New("anthropic: status 400: messages.1: invalid request"),
	}
	hooks := taskLLMStreamHooks{
		current: func(ctx context.Context) (taskLLMSelection, error) {
			return taskLLMSelection{profileID: 11, provider: provider}, nil
		},
		exhaust: func(taskLLMSelection, error) (db.TaskLLMTransition, error) {
			return db.TaskLLMTransition{}, nil
		},
	}
	_, err := collectTaskLLMStream(streamTaskLLM(context.Background(), "7", llm.CompletionRequest{}, hooks))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected the deterministic rejection to surface")
	}
	if provider.calls != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("deterministic 4xx must not be retried: provider calls=%d, want 1", provider.calls)
	}
}

// A role with no Agent binding falls through to the task chain, then to global —
// and an exhausted chain stays a hard stop instead of silently borrowing global.
func TestTaskRuntimeAvailableUnboundRoleFollowsChainThenGlobal(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	// A nil pg means effectiveProfileForAgent finds no binding for any role, so
	// every role here resolves through the chain/global levels.
	s := &Server{m: &Manager{}}
	task := &Task{ID: "7"}

	if s.taskRuntimeAvailable(task, "worker") {
		t.Fatal("no binding, no chain and no global provider must not be runnable")
	}

	if !s.taskRuntimeAvailable(task, "worker") {
		t.Fatal("global provider must serve a role with no binding and no chain")

	}

	task.setLLMState(&profileID, nil, []int64{profileID}, 1, "chain_exhausted", "quota exhausted")
	if s.taskRuntimeAvailable(task, "worker") {
		t.Fatal("exhausted chain must not fall back to the global provider")
	}
}

func TestProfileDeleteRestoresQuotaBlockedIntentWhenFallbackAvailable(t *testing.T) {
	m, err := NewManager(t.TempDir(), "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) - skipping", err)
	}
	defer m.Close()

	profileID, err := m.pg.SaveProfile(&db.LLMProfile{
		Name:   fmt.Sprintf("delete-quota-fallback-%d", time.Now().UnixNano()),
		Format: "openai",
		Model:  "test-model",
		APIKey: "test-key",
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	task, err := m.CreateTaskWithOptions("quota fallback", "resume intent", db.TaskCreateOptions{
		LLMProfileIDs: []int64{profileID},
	})
	if err != nil {
		_ = m.pg.DeleteProfile(profileID)
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		_, _ = m.DeleteTask(task.ID, DeleteTaskOptions{})
		_ = m.pg.DeleteProfile(profileID)
	})

	intentID, err := task.Store.AddIntent(map[string]any{"action": "retry after fallback"}, 1, nil, "planner")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	taskID, err := parseTaskID(task.ID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if transition, err := m.pg.MarkTaskLLMProfileQuotaExhausted(taskID, profileID, "insufficient_quota"); err != nil || !transition.ChainExhausted {
		t.Fatalf("exhaust task chain: transition=%+v err=%v", transition, err)
	}
	if err := task.Store.SetIntentBlockedReason(intentID, db.IntentBlockedLLMQuota); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	task.Paused = true
	if err := m.SetTaskPaused(task.ID, true); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	// Removing the final explicit entry restores the legacy/global fallback. The
	// post-delete sync must reopen only quota-blocked work without unpausing it.
	if err := m.pg.DeleteProfile(profileID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s := &Server{
		m:             m,
		llmOn:         true,
		llmProv:       &scriptedLLMProvider{},
		provByProfile: map[int64]*provEntry{},
	}
	s.restoreTasksAfterProfileDelete(m.pg)

	node, err := task.Store.GetNode(intentID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if node == nil || node.State != "open" || node.BlockedReason != "" {
		t.Fatalf("quota-blocked intent was not reopened: %+v", node)
	}
	if !task.Paused {
		t.Fatal("profile deletion must not resume a paused task")
	}
	state := task.llmStateSnapshot()
	if len(state.ProfileIDs) != 0 || state.FailoverState != "default" {
		t.Fatalf("task did not return to fallback state: %+v", state)
	}
}

=====================================================================
FILE: server/task_metadata.go
=====================================================================
package server

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

const (
	maxTaskNameRunes           = 200
	maxTaskMetadataRequestSize = 16 << 10
)

// updateTaskMetadata changes list-only task metadata. It intentionally does not
// touch lifecycle state, scheduling, or the task's immutable description/goal.
func (s *Server) updateTaskMetadata(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	taskID := r.PathValue("id")
	if _, ok := s.m.Task(taskID); !ok {
		writeErr(w, http.StatusNotFound, "task not found")
		return
	}
	r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxTaskMetadataRequestSize)
	var request struct {
		Name          *string `json:"name"`
		Pinned        *bool   `json:"pinned"`
		PlanQuietMode *bool   `json:"plan_quiet_mode"`
		TargetGate    *bool   `json:"target_gate"`
	}
	if err := decode(r, &request); err != nil {
		var tooLarge *http.MaxBytesError
		if errors.As(err, &tooLarge) {
			writeErr(w, http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge, "request body too large")
		} else {
			writeErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		}
		return
	}
	if request.Name == nil && request.Pinned == nil && request.PlanQuietMode == nil && request.TargetGate == nil {
		writeErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "at least one of name, pinned, plan_quiet_mode or target_gate must be provided")
		return
	}
	if request.Name != nil {
		name := strings.TrimSpace(*request.Name)
		if name == "" {
			writeErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "task name cannot be empty")
			return
		}
		if utf8.RuneCountInString(name) > maxTaskNameRunes {
			writeErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, fmt.Sprintf("task name must be at most %d characters", maxTaskNameRunes))
			return
		}
		request.Name = &name
	}
	task, err := s.m.UpdateTaskMetadata(taskID, db.TaskPatch{Name: request.Name, Pinned: request.Pinned, PlanQuietMode: request.PlanQuietMode, TargetGate: request.TargetGate})
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
		return
	}
	if task == nil {
		writeErr(w, http.StatusNotFound, "task not found")
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, taskDTO(task, s.resolvedTaskStatus(task)))
}

	}

		t.Fatal(err)
	}

		t.Fatalf("batch delete response=%+v", response.Items)
	}

			t.Fatalf("conversation %d still exists: %+v err=%v", id, conversation, err)
		}
	}
	if response.Items[1].Error == "" {
		t.Fatalf("missing conversation %s must include an error", fmt.Sprint(missing))
	}
}

package server

import (
	"database/sql"
	"errors"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"strconv"
)

// taskOutcome returns one task's production and cost baseline. It is the
// measurement layer for later RSI comparisons (harness2, Google Research,
// arXiv 2610.14224): nothing here changes agent behavior.
func (s *Server) taskOutcome(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, err := strconv.ParseInt(r.PathValue("id"), 10, 64)
	if err != nil || id <= 0 {
		writeErr(w, 400, "invalid task id")
		return
	}
	outcome, err := s.m.PG().TaskOutcome(r.Context(), id)
	if errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
		writeErr(w, 404, "task not found")
		return
	}
	if err != nil {
		log.Printf("[tasks] outcome query failed for %d: %v", id, err)
		writeErr(w, 500, "outcome query failed")
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, 200, outcome)
}

=====================================================================
FILE: server/task_pause_deadline_test.go
=====================================================================
package server

import (
	"database/sql"
	"strconv"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

// Pausing a task must freeze its wall-clock timeout budget: the admission that
// ends the pause credits the paused interval back onto deadline_at, so a task
// paused overnight (or while the machine is off) resumes with its remaining
// time instead of immediately settling into the timeout terminal state (#1).
func TestPauseShiftsTaskDeadlineOnResume(t *testing.T) {
	s, _, _ := trafficEvidenceServer(t)
	m := s.m
	pg := s.m.pg

	task, err := m.CreateTask("pause deadline test", "verify the deadline is frozen while paused", nil, 3600, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	id, err := strconv.ParseInt(task.ID, 10, 64)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM tasks WHERE id=$1`, id) })

	// A running task with a stamped deadline (first_run_at + 1h budget).
	if _, err := m.StampTaskFirstRun(task.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := pg.Exec(`UPDATE tasks SET status='running' WHERE id=$1`, id); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var before time.Time
	if err := pg.QueryRow(`SELECT deadline_at FROM tasks WHERE id=$1`, id).Scan(&before); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	// Pause stamps paused_at alongside the user pause.
	if err := m.ApplyTaskPause(task.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var pausedAt sql.NullTime
	if err := pg.QueryRow(`SELECT paused_at FROM tasks WHERE id=$1`, id).Scan(&pausedAt); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !pausedAt.Valid || pausedAt.Time.After(time.Now()) {
		t.Fatalf("pause should stamp paused_at at the current time, got %v", pausedAt.Time)
	}

	// Keep the task parked long enough for the credited interval to be measurable.
	const paused = 1100 * time.Millisecond
	time.Sleep(paused)

	// Admission out of the paused state (a paused task keeps its lifecycle status).
	if err := m.ApplyTaskAdmission(task.ID, "running", "running", false, "resume", false); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	var after time.Time
	var cleared sql.NullTime
	if err := pg.QueryRow(`SELECT deadline_at, paused_at FROM tasks WHERE id=$1`, id).Scan(&after, &cleared); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if shifted := after.Sub(before); shifted < paused-100*time.Millisecond {
		t.Fatalf("resume should credit the paused interval onto the deadline, got shift=%v (paused=%v)", shifted, paused)
	}
	if cleared.Valid {
		t.Fatalf("admission should clear paused_at, got %v", cleared.Time)
	}
	// The live handle must mirror the shifted deadline (the engine clock context
	// is built from it).
	if got := task.lifecycleSnapshot().DeadlineAt; got != after.Unix() {
		t.Fatalf("live handle deadline = %d, want the shifted %d", got, after.Unix())
	}
}

FILE: server/task_resolution.go

package server

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

type taskLLMResolution struct {
	ProfileID *int64 `json:"profile_id,omitempty"`
	Name      string `json:"name"`
	Format    string `json:"format"`
	Model     string `json:"model"`
	Source    string `json:"source"`
	Available bool   `json:"available"`
	Reason    string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
}

func (s *Server) resolutionFromProfile(p *db.LLMProfile, source string) taskLLMResolution {
	if p == nil {
		return taskLLMResolution{Source: source, Reason: "LLM profile does not exist"}
	}
	id := p.ID
	result := taskLLMResolution{
		ProfileID: &id,
		Name:      p.Name,
		Format:    p.Format,
		Model:     p.Model,
		Source:    source,
	}
	// Ollama profiles are keyless by design; the other formats need a key.
	if p.APIKey == "" && p.Format != "ollama" {
		result.Reason = "LLM profile has no API Key set"
		return result
	}
	if _, _, ok := s.providerForProfile(p.ID); !ok {
		result.Reason = "LLM profile format or parameters are invalid"
		return result
	}
	result.Available = true
	return result
}

// resolveTaskRoleLLM mirrors taskLLMRuntime.current without creating a provider:
// role Agent binding -> explicit task chain -> active/global environment config.
// Database failures are returned rather than represented as an unavailable model.
func (s *Server) resolveTaskRoleLLM(t *Task, agentKey string) (taskLLMResolution, error) {
	if s == nil || s.m == nil || s.m.pg == nil {
		return taskLLMResolution{}, fmt.Errorf("database unavailable")
	}
	a, err := s.m.pg.GetAgentByKey(agentKey)
	if err != nil {
		return taskLLMResolution{}, fmt.Errorf("load agent %q: %w", agentKey, err)
	}
	if a != nil && a.LLMProfileID != nil {
		p, err := s.m.pg.ProfileByID(*a.LLMProfileID)
		if err != nil {
			return taskLLMResolution{}, fmt.Errorf("load agent LLM profile: %w", err)
		}
		if p != nil {
			resolved := s.resolutionFromProfile(p, "agent_binding")
			if resolved.Available {
				return resolved, nil
			}
		}
	}
	state := t.llmStateSnapshot()
	if len(state.ProfileIDs) > 0 {
		if state.ActiveID == nil {
			return taskLLMResolution{Source: "task_chain", Reason: "task LLM profile chain quota exhausted"}, nil
		}
		p, err := s.m.pg.ProfileByID(*state.ActiveID)
		if err != nil {
			return taskLLMResolution{}, fmt.Errorf("load task LLM profile: %w", err)
		}
		return s.resolutionFromProfile(p, "task_chain"), nil
	}
	p, err := s.m.pg.ActiveProfile()
	if err != nil {
		return taskLLMResolution{}, fmt.Errorf("load global LLM profile: %w", err)
	}
	if p != nil {
		resolved := s.resolutionFromProfile(p, "global_profile")
		if resolved.Available {
			return resolved, nil
		}
	}
	s.cfgMu.Lock()
	on, name, cfg := s.llmOn, s.llmProf, s.llmCfg
	s.cfgMu.Unlock()
	if on {
		if name == "" {
			name = "global configuration"
		}
		return taskLLMResolution{
			Name: name, Format: cfg.Provider(), Model: cfg.Model,
			Source: "environment", Available: true,
		}, nil
	}
	return taskLLMResolution{Source: "global", Reason: "no available LLM profile"}, nil
}

func (s *Server) taskLLMResolutionHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	t, ok := s.m.Task(r.PathValue("id"))
	if !ok {
		writeErr(w, 404, "task not found")
		return
	}
	roles := map[string]taskLLMResolution{}
	for responseKey, agentKey := range map[string]string{
		"mainagent": "mainagent",
		"planner":   "planner",
		"worker":    "worker",
	} {
		resolved, err := s.resolveTaskRoleLLM(t, agentKey)
		if err != nil {
			writeErr(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
			return
		}
		roles[responseKey] = resolved
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, roles)
}

FILE: server/task_scope_description_test.go

package server

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/agent"
)

// PG: on an existing database whose add_task_scope row still holds the old
// "authorization boundary" text, the startup seeders replace it with the code
// description; an operator-edited description is preserved; a second run changes
// nothing; and ToolResolve then serves the new description to the model.
func TestTaskScopeDescriptionUpgrade(t *testing.T) {
	skipWithoutDSN(t)
	m, err := NewManager(t.TempDir(), "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { m.Close() })
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	cancel()
	s := New(ctx, m, t.TempDir(), t.TempDir(), t.TempDir())
	t.Cleanup(func() { agent.SetToolResolve(nil) })
	pg := m.pg

	var want string
	for _, seed := range agent.BuiltinToolSeeds() {
		if seed.Key == "add_task_scope" {
			want = seed.Desc
		}
	}
	if want == "" || want == oldTaskScopeDescription {
		t.Fatalf("precondition: code description must exist and differ from the old text: %q", want)
	}

	old, err := pg.GetTool("add_task_scope")
	if err != nil || old == nil {
		t.Fatal("missing add_task_scope", err)
	}
	bindings, _ := json.Marshal(old.Agents)
	t.Cleanup(func() { pg.UpdateTool(old.Key, old.Description, old.Schema, bindings, old.Enabled) })

	snapshot := func() (string, time.Time) {
		var desc string
		var upd time.Time
		if err := pg.QueryRow(`SELECT description, updated_at FROM tools WHERE key='add_task_scope'`).Scan(&desc, &upd); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return desc, upd
	}

	// An existing install still holding the old seeded text is upgraded.
	if err := pg.UpdateTool("add_task_scope", oldTaskScopeDescription, old.Schema, bindings, true); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s.seedOrchestrationTools()
	desc1, upd1 := snapshot()
	if desc1 != want {
		t.Fatalf("old description not replaced: %q", desc1)
	}
	s.seedOrchestrationTools()
	desc2, upd2 := snapshot()
	if desc2 != desc1 || !upd2.Equal(upd1) {
		t.Fatalf("second run changed the row: %q %v -> %q %v", desc1, upd1, desc2, upd2)
	}
	if got := resolvedTaskScopeDescription(t); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("ToolResolve serves %q, want the new description", got)
	}

	// An operator-edited description is left alone.
	if err := pg.UpdateTool("add_task_scope", "operator description", old.Schema, bindings, true); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s.seedOrchestrationTools()
	if desc, _ := snapshot(); desc != "operator description" {
		t.Fatalf("operator description overwritten: %q", desc)
	}
}

// resolvedTaskScopeDescription returns add_task_scope's description as
// ToolResolve serves it to the planner.
func resolvedTaskScopeDescription(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	tools := agent.ToolResolve()(context.Background(), "planner", agent.NewToolSet(nil, "").PlannerTools())
	for _, tl := range tools {
		if tl.Name() == "add_task_scope" {
			return tl.Description()
		}
	}
	t.Fatal("planner lost add_task_scope")
	return ""
}

FILE: server/task_templates.go

package server

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

const maxTaskTemplateRequestBytes = 512 << 10

// taskTemplateRequest uses pointers so PATCH can distinguish omitted fields from
// explicit empty values. Empty values are still rejected by the DB validator.
// category_id / intercept_rules presence is detected via the raw key set (see
// decodeTaskTemplateRequest) so a PATCH can clear category to null.
type taskTemplateRequest struct {
	Name           *string                `json:"name"`
	Description    *string                `json:"description"`
	Goal           *string                `json:"goal"`
	CategoryID     *int64                 `json:"category_id"`
	InterceptRules []taskInterceptRuleReq `json:"intercept_rules"`
}

// decodeTaskTemplateRequest decodes the body into req and returns the set of
// top-level keys present in the JSON (for PATCH presence detection).
func decodeTaskTemplateRequest(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, req *taskTemplateRequest) (map[string]struct{}, bool) {
	r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxTaskTemplateRequestBytes)
	body, err := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
	if err != nil {
		var tooLarge *http.MaxBytesError
		if errors.As(err, &tooLarge) {
			writeErr(w, http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge, "request body too large")
		} else {
			writeErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		}
		return nil, false
	}
	var raw map[string]json.RawMessage
	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &raw); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return nil, false
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, req); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return nil, false
	}
	present := make(map[string]struct{}, len(raw))
	for k := range raw {
		present[k] = struct{}{}
	}
	return present, true
}

func validateTaskTemplateRequest(req taskTemplateRequest) error {
	checks := []struct {
		name  string
		value *string
		limit int
	}{
		{name: "name", value: req.Name, limit: db.MaxTaskTemplateNameRunes},
		{name: "description", value: req.Description, limit: db.MaxTaskTemplateTextRunes},
		{name: "goal", value: req.Goal, limit: db.MaxTaskTemplateTextRunes},
	}
	for _, check := range checks {
		if check.value == nil {
			continue
		}
		value := strings.TrimSpace(*check.value)
		if check.name == "name" {
			value = strings.Join(strings.Fields(value), " ")
		}
		if utf8.RuneCountInString(value) > check.limit {
			return fmt.Errorf("%s must be at most %d characters", check.name, check.limit)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func writeTaskTemplateErr(w http.ResponseWriter, err error) {
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, db.ErrTaskTemplateInvalid):
		writeErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
	case errors.Is(err, db.ErrTaskTemplateNameConflict):
		writeErr(w, http.StatusConflict, "template name already exists")
	case errors.Is(err, db.ErrTaskTemplateNotFound):
		writeErr(w, http.StatusNotFound, "task template not found")
	default:
		writeErr(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
	}
}

func (s *Server) pgListTaskTemplates(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
	pg := s.pg(w)
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	templates, err := pg.ListTaskTemplates()
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"templates": templates})
}

func (s *Server) pgCreateTaskTemplate(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	pg := s.pg(w)
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	var req taskTemplateRequest
	if _, ok := decodeTaskTemplateRequest(w, r, &req); !ok {
		return
	}
	if err := validateTaskTemplateRequest(req); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return
	}
	rules, err := buildTaskInterceptRules(req.InterceptRules)
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid intercept/allow rule: "+err.Error())
		return
	}
	template, err := pg.CreateTaskTemplate(db.TaskTemplateInput{
		Name:           stringValue(req.Name),
		Description:    stringValue(req.Description),
		Goal:           stringValue(req.Goal),
		CategoryID:     req.CategoryID,
		InterceptRules: rules,
	})
	if err != nil {
		writeTaskTemplateErr(w, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, template)
}

func (s *Server) pgUpdateTaskTemplate(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	pg := s.pg(w)
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	id, ok := pathInt(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		writeErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "bad task template id")
		return
	}
	var req taskTemplateRequest
	present, ok := decodeTaskTemplateRequest(w, r, &req)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	if err := validateTaskTemplateRequest(req); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return
	}
	_, catPresent := present["category_id"]
	_, rulesPresent := present["intercept_rules"]
	if req.Name == nil && req.Description == nil && req.Goal == nil && !catPresent && !rulesPresent {
		writeErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "at least one of name, description, goal, category_id, or intercept_rules is required")
		return
	}
	patch := db.TaskTemplatePatch{Name: req.Name, Description: req.Description, Goal: req.Goal}
	if catPresent {
		patch.SetCategoryID = true
		patch.CategoryID = req.CategoryID
	}
	if rulesPresent {
		rules, err := buildTaskInterceptRules(req.InterceptRules)
		if err != nil {
			writeErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid intercept/allow rules: "+err.Error())
			return
		}
		patch.SetInterceptRules = true
		patch.InterceptRules = rules
	}
	template, err := pg.PatchTaskTemplate(id, patch)
	if err != nil {
		writeTaskTemplateErr(w, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, template)
}

func (s *Server) pgDeleteTaskTemplate(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	pg := s.pg(w)
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	id, ok := pathInt(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		writeErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "bad task template id")
		return
	}
	deleted, err := pg.DeleteTaskTemplate(id)
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
		return
	}
	if !deleted {
		writeErr(w, http.StatusNotFound, "task template not found")
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"deleted": id})
}

func stringValue(value *string) string {
	if value == nil {
		return ""
	}
	return *value
}

package server

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

func TestTaskTemplateHTTPCRUD(t *testing.T) {
	m, err := NewManager(t.TempDir(), "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) — skipping", err)
	}
	defer m.Close()
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	s := New(ctx, m, t.TempDir(), t.TempDir(), t.TempDir())
	defer stopTestServer(t, s, cancel)
	h := s.Handler()
	token, err := signJWT(s.jwtKey)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	do := func(method, path string, body any) (int, map[string]any) {
		var data []byte
		if body != nil {
			data, _ = json.Marshal(body)
		}
		req := httptest.NewRequest(method, path, bytes.NewReader(data))
		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
		rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
		h.ServeHTTP(rec, req)
		var out map[string]any
		_ = json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &out)
		return rec.Code, out
	}

	name := fmt.Sprintf("http-template-%d", time.Now().UnixNano())
	code, created := do(http.MethodPost, "/api/task-templates", map[string]any{
		"name": name, "description": "description", "goal": "goal",
	})
	if code != http.StatusCreated {
		t.Fatalf("create status=%d body=%v", code, created)
	}
	id := int64(created["id"].(float64))
	t.Cleanup(func() { _, _ = m.pg.DeleteTaskTemplate(id) })

	code, duplicate := do(http.MethodPost, "/api/task-templates", map[string]any{
		"name": "  " + name + "  ", "description": "other", "goal": "other",
	})
	if code != http.StatusConflict {
		t.Fatalf("duplicate status=%d body=%v", code, duplicate)
	}

	code, updated := do(http.MethodPatch, fmt.Sprintf("/api/task-templates/%d", id), map[string]any{"goal": "patched goal"})
	if code != http.StatusOK || updated["goal"] != "patched goal" || updated["description"] != "description" {
		t.Fatalf("patch status=%d body=%v", code, updated)
	}
	code, _ = do(http.MethodPatch, fmt.Sprintf("/api/task-templates/%d", id), map[string]any{
		"goal": strings.Repeat("x", db.MaxTaskTemplateTextRunes+1),
	})
	if code != http.StatusBadRequest {
		t.Fatalf("overlong patch status=%d, want %d", code, http.StatusBadRequest)
	}
	code, _ = do(http.MethodPost, "/api/task-templates", map[string]any{
		"name": "oversized", "description": strings.Repeat("x", maxTaskTemplateRequestBytes+1), "goal": "goal",
	})
	if code != http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge {
		t.Fatalf("oversized create status=%d, want %d", code, http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge)
	}
	code, listed := do(http.MethodGet, "/api/task-templates", nil)
	if code != http.StatusOK || listed["templates"] == nil {
		t.Fatalf("list status=%d body=%v", code, listed)
	}
	code, deleted := do(http.MethodDelete, fmt.Sprintf("/api/task-templates/%d", id), nil)
	if code != http.StatusOK || int64(deleted["deleted"].(float64)) != id {
		t.Fatalf("delete status=%d body=%v", code, deleted)
	}
}

func TestConversationPatchReturnsPinState(t *testing.T) {

		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) — skipping", err)

	token, err := signJWT(s.jwtKey)
	if err != nil {

		t.Fatalf("patch status=%d body=%s", rec.Code, rec.Body.String())

		Title    string  `json:"title"`
		Pinned   bool    `json:"pinned"`
		PinnedAt *string `json:"pinned_at"`

		t.Fatal(err)

		t.Fatalf("unexpected conversation patch response: %+v", updated)
	}

	body, _ = json.Marshal(map[string]any{"title": strings.Repeat("x", maxConversationTitleRunes+1)})

	req = httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPatch, fmt.Sprintf("/api/conversations/%d", conversation.ID), bytes.NewReader(body))
	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
	rec = httptest.NewRecorder()
	s.Handler().ServeHTTP(rec, req)
	if rec.Code != http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge {
		t.Fatalf("oversized conversation patch status=%d body=%s", rec.Code, rec.Body.String())
	}

	body, _ = json.Marshal(map[string]any{
		"agent_key": "mainagent", "title": strings.Repeat("x", maxConversationTitleRunes+1),
	})
	req = httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/api/conversations", bytes.NewReader(body))
	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
	rec = httptest.NewRecorder()
	s.Handler().ServeHTTP(rec, req)
	if rec.Code != http.StatusBadRequest {
		t.Fatalf("overlong conversation create status=%d body=%s", rec.Code, rec.Body.String())

	body, _ = json.Marshal(map[string]any{
		"agent_key": "mainagent", "title": strings.Repeat("x", maxConversationRequestBytes+1),
	})
	req = httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/api/conversations", bytes.NewReader(body))
	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
	rec = httptest.NewRecorder()
	s.Handler().ServeHTTP(rec, req)
	if rec.Code != http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge {
		t.Fatalf("oversized conversation create status=%d body=%s", rec.Code, rec.Body.String())
	}
}

package server

import (
	"database/sql"
	"os"
	"testing"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
	_ "github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib"
)

// TestMain acquires a PostgreSQL advisory lock (7337741002) for the entire
// server test suite so cross-package DELETE cleanup races with db/agent
// packages are avoided when running `go test ./...`.
func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
	// Own database per package (#80): with separate databases, packages stop
	// contending on shared tables and the advisory lock below stops
	// serializing go test ./... across packages.
	db.SuffixTestDatabase("server")
	// Fixed test key via env: NewManager's InitSecrets then writes no key file.
	os.Setenv("HIVE_SECRET_KEY", "MDEyMzQ1Njc4OWFiY2RlZjAxMjM0NTY3ODlhYmNkZWY=")
	dsn, _, err := db.DSN()
	if err != nil {
		os.Exit(m.Run())
	}
	conn, err := sql.Open("pgx", dsn)
	if err != nil || conn.Ping() != nil {
		os.Exit(m.Run())
	}
	defer conn.Close()
	if _, err := conn.Exec(`SELECT pg_advisory_lock(7337741002)`); err != nil {
		os.Exit(m.Run())
	}
	defer conn.Exec(`SELECT pg_advisory_unlock(7337741002)`) //nolint:errcheck
	os.Exit(m.Run())
}

// skipWithoutDSN skips the test when neither HIVE_PG_DSN nor a config file
// supplies a database, so fixtures that t.Fatal on a NewManager error skip
// instead of failing. A configured database that cannot be reached still fails.
func skipWithoutDSN(t *testing.T) {
	t.Helper()
	if _, _, err := db.DSN(); err != nil {
		t.Skipf("no database config (%v) — skipping", err)
	}
}

package server

import (
	"context"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

// stopTestServer cancels a test server's context and joins what New started.
// New restores every unfinished task in the shared database and runs its
// planner, worker and deadline loops, which write under m.dir. Call it with
// defer right after New, so it runs before m.Close and the TempDir cleanups.
func stopTestServer(t *testing.T, s *Server, cancel context.CancelFunc) {
	t.Helper()
	cancel()
	for _, task := range s.m.List() {
		s.engine.BeginDelete(task.ID)
		waitCtx, waitCancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
		if err := s.waitTaskQuiescent(waitCtx, task.ID); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("task %s still running at teardown: %v", task.ID, err)
		}
		waitCancel()
		s.engine.StopTask(task.ID)
	}
	s.archiveWG.Wait()
	<-s.side.done
}

package server

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"log"

	actool "github.com/Autumn-27/norma/tool"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/agent"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

type toolUsageRecorder interface {
	InsertToolUsage(*db.ToolUsage) error
}

// meteredTool records one row immediately before a catalog tool is invoked. It
// embeds the resolved tool so schema overrides, defaults and permission behavior
// remain unchanged.
type meteredTool struct {
	actool.CoreTool
	recorder toolUsageRecorder
	toolKey  string
	agentKey string
	ri       agent.RunInfo
}

func meterTool(t actool.CoreTool, recorder toolUsageRecorder, toolKey, agentKey string, ri agent.RunInfo) actool.CoreTool {
	if recorder == nil {
		return t
	}
	return &meteredTool{CoreTool: t, recorder: recorder, toolKey: toolKey, agentKey: agentKey, ri: ri}
}

func (m *meteredTool) Call(ctx context.Context, input json.RawMessage, tc *actool.ToolContext) (actool.Result, error) {
	if err := m.recorder.InsertToolUsage(&db.ToolUsage{
		ToolKey:       m.toolKey,
		AgentKey:      m.agentKey,
		TaskID:        m.ri.TaskID,
		ExplorationID: m.ri.ExplorationID,
		IntentID:      m.ri.IntentID,
		SessionID:     m.ri.SessionID,
	}); err != nil {
		log.Printf("[toolusage] insert %s: %v", m.toolKey, err)
	}
	return m.CoreTool.Call(ctx, input, tc)
}

package server

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"testing"

	actool "github.com/Autumn-27/norma/tool"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/agent"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

type recordingToolUsage struct {
	rows []*db.ToolUsage
	err  error
}

func (r *recordingToolUsage) InsertToolUsage(row *db.ToolUsage) error {
	copy := *row
	r.rows = append(r.rows, &copy)
	return r.err
}

func TestMeterToolRecordsAttributionAndDelegates(t *testing.T) {
	calls := 0
	base := actool.Build(actool.Spec{
		Name: "record_fact",
		Run: func(context.Context, json.RawMessage, *actool.ToolContext) (actool.Result, error) {
			calls++
			return actool.Result{}, nil
		},
	})
	recorder := &recordingToolUsage{}
	ri := agent.RunInfo{TaskID: 42, ExplorationID: 8, IntentID: 9, SessionID: "session-1"}
	wrapped := meterTool(base, recorder, "record_fact", "worker", ri)

	if _, err := wrapped.Call(context.Background(), json.RawMessage(`{"secret":"not persisted"}`), nil); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if calls != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("delegate calls: want 1, got %d", calls)
	}
	if len(recorder.rows) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("usage rows: want 1, got %d", len(recorder.rows))
	}
	got := recorder.rows[0]
	if got.ToolKey != "record_fact" || got.AgentKey != "worker" || got.TaskID != 42 ||
		got.ExplorationID != 8 || got.IntentID != 9 || got.SessionID != "session-1" {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected attribution: %+v", got)
	}
}

func TestMeterToolFailureDoesNotBreakInvocation(t *testing.T) {
	calls := 0
	base := actool.Build(actool.Spec{
		Name: "list_facts",
		Run: func(context.Context, json.RawMessage, *actool.ToolContext) (actool.Result, error) {
			calls++
			return actool.Result{}, nil
		},
	})
	recorder := &recordingToolUsage{err: errors.New("ledger unavailable")}
	wrapped := meterTool(base, recorder, "list_facts", "worker", agent.RunInfo{})

	if _, err := wrapped.Call(context.Background(), nil, nil); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("metering error leaked into tool call: %v", err)
	}
	if calls != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("delegate calls: want 1, got %d", calls)
	}
}

FILE: server/tools_secrets_api_test.go

package server

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"sync/atomic"
	"testing"
)

// A placeholder keeps the stored secret only for the url and kind it was saved
// with: a changed destination is refused before any write or request.
func TestCustomToolExecDestinationGuard(t *testing.T) {
	s, _, request := trafficEvidenceServer(t)
	pg := s.m.PG()
	var hits atomic.Int32
	echo := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		hits.Add(1)
		io.WriteString(w, "auth="+r.Header.Get("Authorization"))
	}))
	t.Cleanup(echo.Close)
	t.Cleanup(func() { pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM tools WHERE key LIKE 't_secguard%'`) })
	const secret = "Bearer guard-plain-0001"
	schema := `{"type":"object","properties":{"q":{"type":"string"}}}`
	body := func(kind, url, hdr string) string {
		e, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"method": "GET", "url": url, "headers": map[string]string{"Authorization": hdr}})
		return `{"key":"t_secguard","kind":"` + kind + `","enabled":true,"schema":` + schema + `,"exec":` + string(e) + `}`
	}
	storedExec := func() (url, auth string) {
		tl, err := pg.GetTool("t_secguard")
		if err != nil || tl == nil {
			t.Fatalf("GetTool: %v", err)
		}
		var e struct {
			URL     string            `json:"url"`
			Headers map[string]string `json:"headers"`
		}
		_ = json.Unmarshal(tl.Exec, &e)
		return e.URL, e.Headers["Authorization"]
	}
	if resp := request("POST", "/api/tools/custom", body("http", echo.URL, secret)); resp.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("create: HTTP %d %s", resp.Code, resp.Body.String())
	}
	moved := echo.URL + "/elsewhere"

	// 1. Masked header, changed url: refused, nothing written.
	if resp := request("PUT", "/api/tools/custom/t_secguard", body("http", moved, "__masked__")); resp.Code != 400 {
		t.Fatalf("masked header with a changed url must be refused, got HTTP %d", resp.Code)
	}
	if url, auth := storedExec(); url != echo.URL || auth != secret {
		t.Fatalf("a refused update changed the stored exec: %s %s", url, auth)
	}
	// An empty url against a stored one is a change too.
	if resp := request("PUT", "/api/tools/custom/t_secguard", body("http", "", "__masked__")); resp.Code != 400 {
		t.Fatalf("masked header with an emptied url must be refused, got HTTP %d", resp.Code)
	}

	// 2. Masked header, same url: kept.
	if resp := request("PUT", "/api/tools/custom/t_secguard", body("http", echo.URL, "__masked__")); resp.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("masked header with the same url: HTTP %d %s", resp.Code, resp.Body.String())
	}
	if url, auth := storedExec(); url != echo.URL || auth != secret {
		t.Fatalf("the stored secret was not kept: %s %s", url, auth)
	}

	// 3. Test endpoint, masked header, changed url: refused, no request sent.
	e, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"method": "GET", "url": moved, "headers": map[string]string{"Authorization": "__masked__"}})
	if resp := request("POST", "/api/tools/custom/test", `{"key":"t_secguard","kind":"http","exec":`+string(e)+`}`); resp.Code != 400 {
		t.Fatalf("test endpoint with a changed url must be refused, got HTTP %d %s", resp.Code, resp.Body.String())
	}
	if n := hits.Load(); n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("the echo server received %d request(s); the stored secret left", n)
	}

	// 4. Kind change while keeping a placeholder: refused.
	if resp := request("PUT", "/api/tools/custom/t_secguard", body("command", echo.URL, "__masked__")); resp.Code != 400 {
		t.Fatalf("a kind change with a placeholder must be refused, got HTTP %d", resp.Code)
	}
	if tl, _ := pg.GetTool("t_secguard"); tl == nil || tl.Kind != "http" {
		t.Fatalf("a refused kind change was written: %v", tl)
	}

	// 5. An explicit value with a changed url is allowed.
	if resp := request("PUT", "/api/tools/custom/t_secguard", body("http", moved, "Bearer typed-0002")); resp.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("explicit header with a changed url: HTTP %d %s", resp.Code, resp.Body.String())
	}
	if url, auth := storedExec(); url != moved || auth != "Bearer typed-0002" {
		t.Fatalf("explicit replace not stored: %s %s", url, auth)
	}
}

// A custom tool's exec: headers, proxy and body are masked by GET /api/tools;
// the placeholder keeps the stored value on update and in the test endpoint, a
// create with it is refused, and the executor runs on the clear exec.
func TestCustomToolExecMasking(t *testing.T) {
	s, _, request := trafficEvidenceServer(t)
	pg := s.m.PG()
	echo := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		b, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
		io.WriteString(w, "auth="+r.Header.Get("Authorization")+" body="+string(b))
	}))
	t.Cleanup(echo.Close)
	t.Cleanup(func() { pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM tools WHERE key LIKE 't_secexec%'`) })
	secrets := []string{"hdr-plain-0001", "body-plain-0002", "proxy-plain-0003"}
	schema := `{"type":"object","properties":{"q":{"type":"string"}}}`
	execOf := func(hdr, body, proxy string) string {
		e, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"method": "POST", "url": echo.URL,
			"headers": map[string]string{"Authorization": hdr, "X-Empty": ""}, "body": body, "proxy": proxy})
		return string(e)
	}
	toolBody := func(key, exec string) string {
		return `{"key":"` + key + `","kind":"http","enabled":true,"schema":` + schema + `,"exec":` + exec + `}`
	}
	stored := func() map[string]any {
		tl, err := pg.GetTool("t_secexec")
		if err != nil || tl == nil {
			t.Fatalf("GetTool: %v", err)
		}
		var e map[string]any
		_ = json.Unmarshal(tl.Exec, &e)
		return e
	}

	plain := execOf("Bearer "+secrets[0], secrets[1], "http://u:"+secrets[2]+"@127.0.0.1:1")
	if resp := request("POST", "/api/tools/custom", toolBody("t_secexec", plain)); resp.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("create: HTTP %d %s", resp.Code, resp.Body.String())
	}
	var raw string
	if err := pg.QueryRow(`SELECT exec::text FROM tools WHERE key='t_secexec'`).Scan(&raw); err != nil || !strings.Contains(raw, "__hive_enc") {
		t.Fatalf("exec not sealed at rest: %s %v", raw, err)
	}

	// List: masked with *_set flags, nothing in clear.
	resp := request("GET", "/api/tools", "")
	for _, sec := range secrets {
		if resp.Code != 200 || strings.Contains(resp.Body.String(), sec) {
			t.Fatalf("GET /api/tools: HTTP %d or a secret returned in clear", resp.Code)
		}
	}
	var list struct {
		Tools []struct {
			Key  string          `json:"key"`
			Exec json.RawMessage `json:"exec"`
		}
	}
	_ = json.Unmarshal(resp.Body.Bytes(), &list)
	var masked json.RawMessage
	for _, tl := range list.Tools {
		if tl.Key == "t_secexec" {
			masked = tl.Exec
		}
	}
	var m map[string]any
	_ = json.Unmarshal(masked, &m)
	h, _ := m["headers"].(map[string]any)
	if h["Authorization"] != "__masked__" || h["X-Empty"] != "" || m["body"] != "__masked__" || m["proxy"] != "__masked__" ||
		m["headers_set"] != true || m["body_set"] != true || m["proxy_set"] != true || m["url"] != echo.URL {
		t.Fatalf("exec not masked as expected: %s", masked)
	}

	// Update echoing the masked exec: every stored value is kept, no flag stored.
	if resp := request("PUT", "/api/tools/custom/t_secexec", toolBody("t_secexec", string(masked))); resp.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("update with placeholders: HTTP %d %s", resp.Code, resp.Body.String())
	}
	e := stored()
	if e["headers"].(map[string]any)["Authorization"] != "Bearer "+secrets[0] || e["body"] != secrets[1] ||
		!strings.Contains(e["proxy"].(string), secrets[2]) || e["body_set"] != nil {
		t.Fatalf("placeholders did not keep the stored exec: %v", e)
	}

	// Test endpoint: the saved tool's key resolves the placeholders.
	noProxy := execOf("__masked__", "__masked__", "")
	if resp := request("POST", "/api/tools/custom/test", `{"kind":"http","exec":`+noProxy+`}`); resp.Code != 400 {
		t.Fatalf("a placeholder without a saved tool must be refused, got HTTP %d", resp.Code)
	}
	resp = request("POST", "/api/tools/custom/test", `{"key":"t_secexec","kind":"http","exec":`+noProxy+`}`)
	if resp.Code != 200 || !strings.Contains(resp.Body.String(), "auth=Bearer "+secrets[0]+" body="+secrets[1]) {
		t.Fatalf("test endpoint did not use the stored values: HTTP %d %s", resp.Code, resp.Body.String())
	}

	// Replace the header, keep the body, clear the proxy.
	if resp := request("PUT", "/api/tools/custom/t_secexec", toolBody("t_secexec", execOf("Bearer new-0004", "__masked__", ""))); resp.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("update: HTTP %d %s", resp.Code, resp.Body.String())
	}
	e = stored()
	if e["headers"].(map[string]any)["Authorization"] != "Bearer new-0004" || e["body"] != secrets[1] || e["proxy"] != "" {
		t.Fatalf("replace/keep/clear: %v", e)
	}
	if resp := request("GET", "/api/tools", ""); strings.Contains(resp.Body.String(), "new-0004") {
		t.Fatal("a replaced secret is returned in clear")
	}

	// Create with a placeholder: refused, nothing written.
	for _, ex := range []string{execOf("__masked__", "", ""), execOf("", "__masked__", ""), execOf("", "", "__masked__")} {
		if resp := request("POST", "/api/tools/custom", toolBody("t_secexec_new", ex)); resp.Code != 400 {
			t.Fatalf("create with a placeholder must be refused, got HTTP %d", resp.Code)
		}
	}
	if tl, _ := pg.GetTool("t_secexec_new"); tl != nil {
		t.Fatal("a refused create wrote a row")
	}

	// The executor receives the clear exec from the sealed row.
	tools, err := s.customTools()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, tl := range tools {
		if tl.Name() != "t_secexec" {
			continue
		}
		res, err := tl.Call(context.Background(), json.RawMessage(`{"q":"x"}`), nil)
		if err != nil || !strings.Contains(res.Flatten(), "auth=Bearer new-0004 body="+secrets[1]) {
			t.Fatalf("executor output %q %v", res.Flatten(), err)
		}
		return
	}
	t.Fatal("t_secexec not built by customTools")
}

// The platform tools follow the API: create refuses a placeholder, update keeps the stored value.
func TestPlatformCustomToolPlaceholders(t *testing.T) {
	s, _, _ := trafficEvidenceServer(t)
	pg := s.m.PG()
	t.Cleanup(func() { pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM tools WHERE key LIKE 't_secexec%'`) })
	in := func(exec string) json.RawMessage {
		return json.RawMessage(`{"key":"t_secexec_pt","kind":"command","exec":` + exec + `}`)
	}
	create, update := s.toolCreateCustomTool(), s.toolUpdateCustomTool()
	if res, _ := create.Call(context.Background(), in(`{"command":"echo","proxy":"__masked__"}`), nil); !res.IsError {
		t.Fatalf("create with a placeholder must fail: %s", res.Flatten())
	}
	if res, _ := create.Call(context.Background(), in(`{"command":"echo","body":"pt-body-plain"}`), nil); res.IsError {
		t.Fatalf("create: %s", res.Flatten())
	}
	if res, _ := update.Call(context.Background(), in(`{"command":"echo 2","body":"__masked__"}`), nil); res.IsError {
		t.Fatalf("update: %s", res.Flatten())
	}
	tl, err := pg.GetTool("t_secexec_pt")
	if err != nil || tl == nil || !jsonHas(tl.Exec, "pt-body-plain") || !jsonHas(tl.Exec, "echo 2") {
		t.Fatalf("update with a placeholder must keep the stored body: %v %v", tl, err)
	}
}

func jsonHas(raw json.RawMessage, s string) bool { return strings.Contains(string(raw), s) }

FILE: server/tools_wire_test.go

package server

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"testing"

	actool "github.com/Autumn-27/norma/tool"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/agent"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

func names(tools []actool.CoreTool) map[string]actool.CoreTool {
	m := map[string]actool.CoreTool{}
	for _, t := range tools {
		m[t.Name()] = t
	}
	return m
}

// TestWireTools verifies end-to-end against the live dev PG: wireTools seeds the
// catalog, ToolResolve keeps record_fact for worker but drops it for planner (not
// bound), and an edited description + injected default flow through.
func TestWireTools(t *testing.T) {
	dsn, _, err := db.DSN()
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("no database config (%v) — skipping", err)
	}
	pg, err := db.Open(dsn)
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) — skipping", err)
	}
	defer pg.Close()

	wireTools(pg, nil) // nil domainReg: test only covers filter/decoration, not injection
	t.Cleanup(func() { agent.SetToolResolve(nil) })
	// Prevent interactive-shell Bash decoration: if the worker agent has
	// interactive_shell=true in the DB, ToolResolve would append a note to
	// Bash's description. Disable that for this test so the undecorated
	// pass-through assertion holds regardless of DB state.
	t.Setenv("AGENT_CORE_DISABLE_INTERACTIVE_SHELL", "1")

	// Seeding populated the catalog.
	rf, err := pg.GetTool("record_fact")
	if err != nil || rf == nil {
		t.Fatalf("record_fact not seeded: %v", err)
	}

	// Build a base as the worker does: its domain tools + defaults, resolved for
	// "worker" then for "planner".
	ts := agent.NewToolSet(nil, "")
	base := append(ts.WorkerTools(), actool.DefaultTools()...)
	ctx := context.Background()

	worker := names(agent.ToolResolve()(ctx, "worker", base))
	if _, ok := worker["record_fact"]; !ok {
		t.Error("worker lost record_fact")
	}
	// SDK generic tools aren't seeded → ToolResolve passes them through unchanged
	// (same object, original description — not decorated). No startup prune touches
	// non-catalog rows, so future user-defined custom tools survive too.
	if bash, ok := worker["Bash"]; !ok {
		t.Error("worker lost Bash (should pass through)")
	} else if bash.Description() != actool.NewBash().Description() {
		t.Error("Bash should pass through undecorated, but description changed")
	}
	// planner is not bound to record_fact → resolving a base that contains it drops it.
	planner := names(agent.ToolResolve()(ctx, "planner", base))
	if _, ok := planner["record_fact"]; ok {
		t.Error("planner should not get record_fact (not bound)")
	}

	// Edit description + add a default to a scalar param, then confirm the resolved
	// worker tool reflects both. Restore from code default on cleanup.
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = pg.UpsertToolForce(rf.Key, rf.Description, rf.Schema, mustJSON(rf.Agents)) })
	var schema map[string]any
	_ = json.Unmarshal(rf.Schema, &schema)
	if props, ok := schema["properties"].(map[string]any); ok {
		if conf, ok := props["confidence"].(map[string]any); ok {
			conf["default"] = "inferred"
		}
	}
	edited := mustJSON(schema)
	if err := pg.UpdateTool(rf.Key, "EDITED DESC", edited, mustJSON([]string{"worker"}), true); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	worker2 := names(agent.ToolResolve()(ctx, "worker", base))
	got := worker2["record_fact"]
	if got == nil {
		t.Fatal("record_fact missing after edit")
	}
	if got.Description() != "EDITED DESC" {
		t.Errorf("description = %q, want EDITED DESC", got.Description())
	}
	// Default injection: omit confidence → handler input should carry the default.
	// We can't run the real handler (nil store), but InputSchema must show the default.
	sc := got.InputSchema()
	props := sc["properties"].(map[string]any)
	conf := props["confidence"].(map[string]any)
	if conf["default"] != "inferred" {
		t.Errorf("confidence.default = %v, want inferred", conf["default"])
	}
}

// TestHealListTaskCredentialsSchema: a list_task_credentials row seeded by an older
// build carries "required": [""]. The startup heal drops that key, leaves the rest of
// the row alone, changes nothing on a second run, and touches no other tool.
func TestHealListTaskCredentialsSchema(t *testing.T) {
	dsn, _, err := db.DSN()
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("no database config (%v) — skipping", err)
	}
	pg, err := db.Open(dsn)
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) — skipping", err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { pg.Close() })
	s := &Server{m: &Manager{pg: pg}}

	const key = "list_task_credentials"
	// Other tools the heal must never touch: a normal required list, and the same
	// malformed value under a different key.
	const probeRequired, probeBlank = "heal_probe_required", "heal_probe_blank"
	const broken = `{"type":"object","properties":{},"required":[""]}`

	// The package test DB is shared: put back whatever it held for the real key.
	old, err := pg.GetTool(key)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		if old == nil {
			pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM tools WHERE key=$1`, key)
		} else {
			pg.Exec(`UPDATE tools SET schema=$2::jsonb WHERE key=$1`, key, string(old.Schema))
		}
		pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM tools WHERE key IN ($1,$2)`, probeRequired, probeBlank)
	})
	for k, schema := range map[string]string{
		key:           broken,
		probeRequired: `{"type":"object","properties":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"required":["x"]}`,
		probeBlank:    broken,
	} {
		if _, err := pg.Exec(`INSERT INTO tools(key, description, schema, agents) VALUES ($1, 'legacy row', $2::jsonb, '["worker"]')
ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET schema=EXCLUDED.schema`, k, schema); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}

	type row struct {
		schema, description, agents, updatedAt string
		enabled                                bool
	}
	read := func(k string) row {
		t.Helper()
		var r row
		if err := pg.QueryRow(`SELECT schema::text, description, agents::text, updated_at::text, enabled FROM tools WHERE key=$1`, k).
			Scan(&r.schema, &r.description, &r.agents, &r.updatedAt, &r.enabled); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", k, err)
		}
		return r
	}
	before, beforeRequired, beforeBlank := read(key), read(probeRequired), read(probeBlank)

	s.healListTaskCredentialsSchema()

	healed := read(key)
	var schema map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(healed.schema), &schema); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, ok := schema["required"]; ok {
		t.Fatalf("required survived the heal: %s", healed.schema)
	}
	if schema["type"] != "object" || schema["properties"] == nil {
		t.Errorf("heal dropped more than required: %s", healed.schema)
	}
	if healed.description != before.description || healed.agents != before.agents || healed.enabled != before.enabled {
		t.Errorf("heal changed description/bindings/enabled: %+v -> %+v", before, healed)
	}

	s.healListTaskCredentialsSchema()

	if again := read(key); again != healed {
		t.Errorf("second heal changed the row: %+v -> %+v", healed, again)
	}
	if got := read(probeRequired); got != beforeRequired {
		t.Errorf("heal touched a tool with a non-empty required: %+v -> %+v", beforeRequired, got)
	}
	if got := read(probeBlank); got != beforeBlank {
		t.Errorf("heal touched another tool key: %+v -> %+v", beforeBlank, got)
	}
}

func mustJSON(v any) json.RawMessage {
	b, _ := json.Marshal(v)
	return b
}

=====================================================================
FILE: server/traffic_ingest.go
=====================================================================
package server

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/traffic"
)

// Ingest caps: a browser tab can produce a burst of entries, but the ingest
// path is meant for deliberate operator captures, not bulk sync. Bodies are
// truncated server-side as a second line of defense behind the extension's
// own caps.
const (
	maxIngestBatch    = 50
	maxIngestBodySize = 256 << 10 // 256 KiB per body
)

// ingestTraffic accepts exchanges captured outside the MITM proxy (currently
// the browser extension) into the global traffic store, so operator-driven
// authenticated browsing becomes evidence the same way proxy traffic is.
func (s *Server) ingestTraffic(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	tr := s.m.Traffic()
	if tr == nil {
		writeErr(w, 503, "traffic store is not available")
		return
	}
	var req struct {
		Exchanges []traffic.ExternalExchange `json:"exchanges"`
	}
	if err := json.NewDecoder(http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, 32<<20)).Decode(&req); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 400, "bad json: "+err.Error())
		return
	}
	if len(req.Exchanges) == 0 {
		writeErr(w, 400, "empty exchanges")
		return
	}
	if len(req.Exchanges) > maxIngestBatch {
		writeErr(w, 400, "too many exchanges in one batch")
		return
	}

	ingested, failed := 0, 0
	for _, e := range req.Exchanges {
		e.RequestBody = truncateBody(e.RequestBody)
		e.ResponseBody = truncateBody(e.ResponseBody)
		if err := tr.RecordExternal(e); err != nil {
			failed++
			continue
		}
		ingested++
	}
	writeJSON(w, 200, map[string]any{"ingested": ingested, "failed": failed})
}

func truncateBody(s string) string {
	if len(s) <= maxIngestBodySize {
		return s
	}
	return s[:maxIngestBodySize] + "\n... [truncated by ingest]"
}

package server

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/traffic"
)

// ingestServer wires a Server with a live traffic store, like
// trafficEvidenceServer but without the finding plumbing.
func ingestServer(t *testing.T) (*Server, func(method, path, body string) *httptest.ResponseRecorder) {
	t.Helper()
	skipWithoutDSN(t)
	m, err := NewManager(t.TempDir(), "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { m.Close() })
	m.traffic, err = traffic.Open(filepath.Join(m.dir, "traffic"), ":0")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	cancel()
	s := New(ctx, m, t.TempDir(), t.TempDir(), t.TempDir())
	s.archiveWG.Wait()
	<-s.side.done
	token, err := signJWT(s.jwtKey)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return s, func(method, path, body string) *httptest.ResponseRecorder {
		r := httptest.NewRequest(method, path, strings.NewReader(body))
		r.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
		r.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		w := httptest.NewRecorder()
		s.Handler().ServeHTTP(w, r)
		return w
	}
}

func TestTrafficIngestFlow(t *testing.T) {
	s, request := ingestServer(t)

	body := fmt.Sprintf(`{"exchanges":[
		{"method":"POST","url":"https://api.example.com/v1/login","status":200,
		 "requestHeaders":{"content-type":"application/json"},"requestBody":"{\"u\":\"u1\"}",
		 "responseHeaders":{"content-type":"application/json"},"responseBody":"{\"token\":\"t\"}"},
		{"method":"GET","url":"https://api.example.com/v1/profile","status":200,
		 "requestHeaders":{},"requestBody":"",
		 "responseHeaders":{},"responseBody":"{\"name\":\"n\"}"}
	]}`)
	w := request("POST", "/api/traffic/ingest", body)
	if w.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("ingest status = %d, body = %s", w.Code, w.Body)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(w.Body.String(), `"ingested":2`) || !strings.Contains(w.Body.String(), `"failed":0`) {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected counts: %s", w.Body)
	}

	// Both entries are visible on the normal traffic API, like proxy traffic.
	w = request("GET", "/api/traffic", "")
	if w.Code != 200 || !strings.Contains(w.Body.String(), "api.example.com") {
		t.Fatalf("traffic page after ingest: %d %s", w.Code, w.Body)
	}

	// One bad URL among good ones: the batch reports per-entry failure.
	mixed := `{"exchanges":[
		{"method":"GET","url":"https://good.example.com/ok","status":200,"responseBody":"ok"},
		{"method":"GET","url":"::::","status":200,"responseBody":"bad"}
	]}`
	w = request("POST", "/api/traffic/ingest", mixed)
	if w.Code != 200 || !strings.Contains(w.Body.String(), `"ingested":1`) || !strings.Contains(w.Body.String(), `"failed":1`) {
		t.Fatalf("mixed batch: %d %s", w.Code, w.Body)
	}

	// Guards: empty batch, oversized batch, oversized body truncation.
	if w = request("POST", "/api/traffic/ingest", `{"exchanges":[]}`); w.Code != 400 {
		t.Fatalf("empty batch status = %d", w.Code)
	}
	big := `{"exchanges":[` + strings.Repeat(`{"method":"GET","url":"https://x.example.com/"},`, maxIngestBatch) + `{}]}`
	if w = request("POST", "/api/traffic/ingest", big); w.Code != 400 {
		t.Fatalf("oversized batch status = %d", w.Code)
	}
	trunc := `{"exchanges":[{"method":"GET","url":"https://big.example.com/","status":200,"responseBody":"` + strings.Repeat("x", maxIngestBodySize+1024) + `"}]}`
	w = request("POST", "/api/traffic/ingest", trunc)
	if w.Code != 200 || !strings.Contains(w.Body.String(), `"ingested":1`) {
		t.Fatalf("truncating batch: %d %s", w.Code, w.Body)
	}
	if n, _ := s.m.Traffic().Count(); n != 4 { // 2 + 1 + 1
		t.Fatalf("final count = %d, want 4", n)
	}
}

func TestTrafficIngestRequiresAuth(t *testing.T) {
	s, _ := ingestServer(t)
	r := httptest.NewRequest("POST", "/api/traffic/ingest", strings.NewReader(`{"exchanges":[]}`))
	w := httptest.NewRecorder()
	s.Handler().ServeHTTP(w, r)
	if w.Code != 401 {
		t.Fatalf("unauthenticated ingest status = %d, want 401", w.Code)
	}
}

package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// A long task goal repeated per event was the dominant bloat. These tests pin the
// fix: the task-context header (description + goal) is rendered ONCE per task, no
// matter how many same-task fires are merged.

const longGoal = "Obtain the protected flag of challenge f2-05 and submit it via submit_flag; the ciphertext of this challenge has highly converged, and the flag can only be derived from binary-embedded data..." // stands in for the thousands of characters of inherited facts

func sameTaskFires(n int) []triggeredRun {
	items := make([]triggeredRun, n)
	for i := range items {
		items[i] = triggeredRun{
			agentKey: "tec_benchmark", taskID: 72, taskDesc: "f2-05 reverse engineering", taskGoal: longGoal,
			message: "[Triggered by tool call]\nTool: submit_flag\nArgs: {...}\nResult: {correct:false}", mergeable: true,
		}
	}
	return items
}

func TestMergeAllRunsWritesTaskGoalOnce(t *testing.T) {
	out := mergeAllRuns(sameTaskFires(39))
	if got := strings.Count(out.message, longGoal); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("same-task goal should appear exactly once in a merged-all run, got %d", got)
	}
	if strings.Count(out.message, "── trigger ") < 1 || !strings.Contains(out.message, "trigger 39") {
		t.Fatalf("all 39 event bodies should be present: %q", out.message)
	}
	// A merged run embeds its header inline, so finalTriggerMessage must not re-add it.
	if out.taskDesc != "" || out.taskGoal != "" {
		t.Fatalf("merged run must clear taskDesc/taskGoal to avoid a duplicate header")
	}
	if finalTriggerMessage(out) != out.message {
		t.Fatalf("finalTriggerMessage must not prepend another header for a merged run")
	}
}

func TestMergeAllRunsGroupsInterleavedTasks(t *testing.T) {
	// Fires from two tasks arriving interleaved (A,B,A,B) must still carry each
	// task's context exactly once — grouping, not per-event repetition.
	mk := func(id int64, goal string) triggeredRun {
		return triggeredRun{agentKey: "a", taskID: id, taskDesc: "d", taskGoal: goal, message: "body", mergeable: true}
	}
	out := mergeAllRuns([]triggeredRun{mk(1, "GOAL_A"), mk(2, "GOAL_B"), mk(1, "GOAL_A"), mk(2, "GOAL_B")})
	if got := strings.Count(out.message, "GOAL_A"); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("task #1 goal should appear once despite interleaving, got %d", got)
	}
	if got := strings.Count(out.message, "GOAL_B"); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("task #2 goal should appear once despite interleaving, got %d", got)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(out.message, "across 2 tasks") {
		t.Fatalf("header should report 2 tasks: %q", out.message)
	}
	if got := strings.Count(out.message, "── trigger "); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("all 4 event bodies should be present, got %d", got)
	}
}

func TestMergeTriggeredRunsWritesTaskGoalOnce(t *testing.T) {
	out := mergeTriggeredRuns(sameTaskFires(5))
	if got := strings.Count(out.message, longGoal); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("same-task goal should appear exactly once in a by-task merge, got %d", got)
	}
}

func TestFinalTriggerMessageSingleFirePrependsHeaderOnce(t *testing.T) {
	item := sameTaskFires(1)[0]
	msg := finalTriggerMessage(item)
	if got := strings.Count(msg, longGoal); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("single fire should carry the task goal exactly once, got %d", got)
	}
	if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "[Task #72") {
		t.Fatalf("single fire should be prefixed with the task-context header: %q", msg)
	}
}

func TestTaskContextHeaderEmptyForIntervalFire(t *testing.T) {
	if h := taskContextHeader(0, "", ""); h != "" {
		t.Fatalf("interval/none trigger (no task) must produce no header, got %q", h)
	}
	// An interval fire's message must pass through untouched.
	item := triggeredRun{message: "interval trigger body"}
	if finalTriggerMessage(item) != "interval trigger body" {
		t.Fatalf("interval fire message must pass through unchanged")
	}
}

func TestTaskContextHeaderTruncatesLongGoal(t *testing.T) {
	huge := strings.Repeat("x", 5000)
	h := taskContextHeader(72, "d", huge)
	if len([]rune(h)) > 800 { // 200 desc + 500 goal + truncation marker/decoration, far below 5000
		t.Fatalf("header should be bounded even for a huge goal, got %d runes", len([]rune(h)))
	}
}

FILE: server/triggers.go

package server

import (
	"net/http"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

// ---------- P3 agent triggers (custom agents only) ----------

func (s *Server) pgListTriggers(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	pg, a, ok := s.agentByKey(w, r)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	trs, err := pg.ListTriggersFor(a.Key)
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 500, err.Error())
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, 200, map[string]any{"triggers": trs})
}

type triggerReq struct {
	Enabled            bool     `json:"enabled"`
	IntervalSec        int      `json:"interval_sec"`
	OnFinding          bool     `json:"on_finding"`
	OnGoalMet          bool     `json:"on_goal_met"`
	OnTaskTimeout      bool     `json:"on_task_timeout"`
	OnToolCall         bool     `json:"on_tool_call"`
	OnTaskCreate       bool     `json:"on_task_create"`
	IntervalMessage    string   `json:"interval_message"`
	FindingMessage     string   `json:"finding_message"`
	GoalMessage        string   `json:"goal_message"`
	TaskTimeoutMessage string   `json:"task_timeout_message"`
	ToolCallMessage    string   `json:"tool_call_message"`
	TaskCreateMessage  string   `json:"task_create_message"`
	ToolNames          []string `json:"tool_names"`
}

// validateTrigger enforces the shared trigger rules for create/update:
// at least one condition, and on_tool_call requires a non-empty tool set.
func validateTrigger(req *triggerReq) string {
	if req.IntervalSec == 0 && !req.OnFinding && !req.OnGoalMet && !req.OnTaskTimeout && !req.OnToolCall && !req.OnTaskCreate {
		return "select at least one trigger condition (interval/finding/goal met/task timeout/tool call/task create)"
	}
	if req.OnToolCall && len(req.ToolNames) == 0 {
		return "tool-call trigger requires selecting at least one tool"
	}
	return ""
}

func (s *Server) pgCreateTrigger(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	pg, a, ok := s.agentByKey(w, r)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	if a.Builtin {
		writeErr(w, 400, "triggers are only supported for custom agents")
		return
	}
	var req triggerReq
	if err := decode(r, &req); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 400, err.Error())
		return
	}
	if req.IntervalSec < 0 {
		req.IntervalSec = 0
	}
	if msg := validateTrigger(&req); msg != "" {
		writeErr(w, 400, msg)
		return
	}
	tr, err := pg.CreateTrigger(&db.AgentTrigger{
		AgentKey: a.Key, Enabled: req.Enabled, IntervalSec: req.IntervalSec,
		OnFinding: req.OnFinding, OnGoalMet: req.OnGoalMet, OnTaskTimeout: req.OnTaskTimeout, OnToolCall: req.OnToolCall, OnTaskCreate: req.OnTaskCreate,
		IntervalMessage: req.IntervalMessage, FindingMessage: req.FindingMessage,
		GoalMessage: req.GoalMessage, TaskTimeoutMessage: req.TaskTimeoutMessage,
		ToolCallMessage: req.ToolCallMessage, TaskCreateMessage: req.TaskCreateMessage, ToolNames: req.ToolNames,
	})
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 500, err.Error())
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, 200, tr)
}

func (s *Server) pgUpdateTrigger(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	pg := s.pg(w)
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	id, ok := pathInt(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		writeErr(w, 400, "bad trigger id")
		return
	}
	var req triggerReq
	if err := decode(r, &req); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 400, err.Error())
		return
	}
	if req.IntervalSec < 0 {
		req.IntervalSec = 0
	}
	if msg := validateTrigger(&req); msg != "" {
		writeErr(w, 400, msg)
		return
	}
	if err := pg.UpdateTrigger(&db.AgentTrigger{
		ID: id, Enabled: req.Enabled, IntervalSec: req.IntervalSec,
		OnFinding: req.OnFinding, OnGoalMet: req.OnGoalMet, OnTaskTimeout: req.OnTaskTimeout, OnToolCall: req.OnToolCall, OnTaskCreate: req.OnTaskCreate,
		IntervalMessage: req.IntervalMessage, FindingMessage: req.FindingMessage,
		GoalMessage: req.GoalMessage, TaskTimeoutMessage: req.TaskTimeoutMessage,
		ToolCallMessage: req.ToolCallMessage, TaskCreateMessage: req.TaskCreateMessage, ToolNames: req.ToolNames,
	}); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 500, err.Error())
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, 200, map[string]any{"ok": true})
}

func (s *Server) pgDeleteTrigger(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	pg := s.pg(w)
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	id, ok := pathInt(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		writeErr(w, 400, "bad trigger id")
		return
	}
	if err := pg.DeleteTrigger(id); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 500, err.Error())
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, 200, map[string]any{"deleted": id})
}

=====================================================================
FILE: server/update_check.go
=====================================================================
package server

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// The update check is opt-in: only HIVE_UPDATE_CHECK=1 (or true/on/yes) lets
// the backend ask the public GitHub releases API for the latest HIVE tag.
// Unset, it makes no request at all and the UI shows no banner.
const updateCheckURL = "https://api.github.com/repos/ProjectZeroDays/EDG-Hive/releases/latest"
const updateCheckInterval = 24 * time.Hour

func updateCheckEnabled() bool {
	switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("HIVE_UPDATE_CHECK"))) {
	case "1", "true", "on", "yes":
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// updateCheck caches the last check (time + latest tag) in memory. A failed
// check also stamps the time, so it is not retried within the same 24 h.
type updateCheck struct {
	enabled   bool
	fetch     func(context.Context) (string, error)
	mu        sync.Mutex
	checkedAt time.Time
	tag       string
}

var updates = &updateCheck{enabled: updateCheckEnabled(), fetch: fetchLatestRelease}

// newerVersion returns the latest release tag when it is newer than current,
// fetching it at most once per updateCheckInterval; "" otherwise.
func (u *updateCheck) newerVersion(ctx context.Context, now time.Time, current string) string {
	if !u.enabled {
		return ""
	}
	u.mu.Lock()
	defer u.mu.Unlock()
	if u.checkedAt.IsZero() || now.Sub(u.checkedAt) >= updateCheckInterval {
		u.checkedAt = now
		u.tag = ""
		if tag, err := u.fetch(ctx); err == nil {
			u.tag = tag
		}
	}
	if u.tag != "" && versionLess(current, u.tag) {
		return u.tag
	}
	return ""
}

// fetchLatestRelease sends only a generic User-Agent: no cookies, no host or
// user identifiers.
func fetchLatestRelease(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, updateCheckURL, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	req.Header.Set("User-Agent", "hive-update-check")
	req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/vnd.github+json")
	resp, err := (&http.Client{Timeout: 5 * time.Second}).Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		return "", errors.New("update check: " + resp.Status)
	}
	var body struct {
		TagName string `json:"tag_name"`
	}
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&body); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return body.TagName, nil // "" shows nothing: parseVersion rejects it
}

// versionLess reports whether a < b, comparing the leading numeric
// major.minor.patch of each ("v2.2.0-3-gabc" reads as 2.2.0). A version
// without a leading number (for example "dev") never compares as older.
func versionLess(a, b string) bool {
	pa, oka := parseVersion(a)
	pb, okb := parseVersion(b)
	if !oka || !okb {
		return false
	}
	for i := range pa {
		if pa[i] != pb[i] {
			return pa[i] < pb[i]
		}
	}
	return false
}

func parseVersion(s string) ([3]int, bool) {
	var out [3]int
	s = strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(s), "v")
	if i := strings.IndexAny(s, "-+"); i >= 0 {
		s = s[:i]
	}
	parts := strings.Split(s, ".")
	if len(parts) > 3 {
		return out, false
	}
	for i, p := range parts {
		n, err := strconv.Atoi(p)
		if err != nil {
			return out, false
		}
		out[i] = n
	}
	return out, true
}

package server

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

func countingFetch(tag string, err error, calls *int) func(context.Context) (string, error) {
	return func(context.Context) (string, error) { *calls++; return tag, err }
}

func TestUpdateCheckOffByDefault(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("HIVE_UPDATE_CHECK", "")
	if updateCheckEnabled() {
		t.Fatal("update check must be off when HIVE_UPDATE_CHECK is unset")
	}
	calls := 0
	u := &updateCheck{enabled: false, fetch: countingFetch("v9.9.9", nil, &calls)}
	if got := u.newerVersion(context.Background(), time.Now(), "2.2.0"); got != "" || calls != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("disabled: got %q with %d fetches, want no banner and no fetch", got, calls)
	}
}

func TestUpdateCheckOncePer24h(t *testing.T) {
	t0 := time.Date(2026, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	calls := 0
	u := &updateCheck{enabled: true, fetch: countingFetch("v2.3.0", nil, &calls)}
	for _, at := range []time.Duration{0, time.Hour, 23*time.Hour + 59*time.Minute} {
		if got := u.newerVersion(context.Background(), t0.Add(at), "2.2.0"); got != "v2.3.0" {
			t.Fatalf("at +%v: got %q, want v2.3.0", at, got)
		}
	}
	if calls != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("fetched %d times within 24h, want 1", calls)
	}
	u.newerVersion(context.Background(), t0.Add(24*time.Hour), "2.2.0")
	if calls != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("fetched %d times after 24h, want 2", calls)
	}
	if got := u.newerVersion(context.Background(), t0.Add(25*time.Hour), "2.3.0"); got != "" {
		t.Fatalf("up to date: got %q, want no banner", got)
	}
}

func TestUpdateCheckFailureShowsNothingAndWaits(t *testing.T) {
	t0 := time.Date(2026, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	calls := 0
	u := &updateCheck{enabled: true, fetch: countingFetch("", errors.New("rate limited"), &calls)}
	for _, at := range []time.Duration{0, time.Minute, 23 * time.Hour} {
		if got := u.newerVersion(context.Background(), t0.Add(at), "2.2.0"); got != "" {
			t.Fatalf("failed check: got %q, want no banner", got)
		}
	}
	if calls != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("failed check retried %d times within 24h, want 1 attempt", calls)
	}
}

func TestVersionLess(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		a, b string
		want bool
	}{
		{"2.2.0", "v2.3.0", true},
		{"v2.2.0", "v2.2.0", false},
		{"2.10.0", "v2.9.0", false},
		{"2.2.0-3-gabc123-dirty", "v2.2.1", true},
		{"dev", "v9.0.0", false},
		{"2.2.0", "not-a-tag", false},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		if got := versionLess(c.a, c.b); got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("versionLess(%q, %q) = %v, want %v", c.a, c.b, got, c.want)
		}
	}
}
